624a92875e66b914: Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78210-8Continuous seismic observations and numerical simulations reveal that, over the past decade, fluid migration and microseismic responses at The Geysers geothermal field have been primarily controlled by heterogeneous permeability.
d2fec18c267cf663: Standard full-waveform inversion (FWI) objective functions often struggle to resolve deep structures when data are dominated by localized near-surface scattering. To address this, we develop a 4-D time-frequency-space-wavenumber (TFXK) objective function that explicitly enforces spatial coherence, leveraging the dense sampling of distributed acoustic sensing. We derive the corresponding adjoint sources for both phase and envelope misfits. By suppressing localized scattering from shallow heterogeneities, the TFXK misfit shifts kernel sensitivity toward deeper, larger scale structural targets. Furthermore, this 4-D mapping smooths the objective function topology, mitigating local minima while improving inversion convergence, as demonstrated in a 2-D synthetic FWI example with strong shallow heterogeneity. The proposed idea of a spatiotemporal objective function is generalizable and can be adapted to other objective functions. We also show how it can accommodate curved fibre geometries via arclength parametrization, Local polynomial Fourier transforms, or a full vectorial wavenumber approach, depending on the complexity of the fibre layout. These mathematical extensions are necessary for applying the method to varied fibre geometries and low-frequency inversions. The foundational principles of our approach extend beyond optical fibres and can also be applied to structural inversions using traditional dense nodal arrays.
3895e2c91b55740a: As the world’s largest continental plate, the deep electrical conductivity structure of the Eurasian continent holds great importance for understanding continental evolution and mantle dynamics. Conventional geomagnetic response functions based on magnetospheric ring current have limited sensitivity in constraining the electrical structure of the upper mantle and transition zone (200–500 km). Previous studies utilizing ionospheric Sq signals considered only the dominant-term transfer functions, neglecting information carried by non-dominant term transfer functions. This study proposes a mantle conductivity structure imaging method based on inverting full-term transfer functions. It incorporates trans-dimensional Bayesian inversion to analyse Sq signals from 14 geomagnetic observatories across Eurasia, thereby obtaining 1-D electrical structures beneath each observatory. Results reveal large lateral heterogeneity in the mantle conductivity structure across Eurasia, with conductivity discontinuities at 100–200 km depth indicating a lithosphere–asthenosphere boundary that progressively deepens from east to west. A distinct conductivity discontinuity at 400–500 km depth beneath eastern Eurasia may result from water transport into the mantle through Western Pacific plate subduction. This research demonstrates the advantage of full-term transfer functions in illuminating mantle conductivity structures, providing new pathways for investigating deep Earth material cycles.
789b7d6afabff975: Underground gas storage (UGS) operations can perturb reservoir conditions and modulate local seismicity, but the temporal evolution of this response under cyclic injection–withdrawal remains poorly constrained. We investigate seismicity around the Serajeh UGS in central Iran by combining 29,781 deep-learning-based single-station earthquake detections, multi-station relocation, centroid moment tensor inversion, and operational records. The relocated hypocentres form a compact cluster near the Serajeh structure, primarily at depths of 3–8 km, overlapping with and extending below the 2.4–3.0 km storage interval. Independent comparison with relocated earthquakes confirms that S–P time at the nearby GHVR station provides a useful first-order proxy for local source distance. Cross-correlation between monthly gas injection and seismicity shows a distinct maximum at an offset of approximately 8 months. This feature is reproduced by the phase-randomized ReshuffleCorr analysis, while additional structure-preserving tests indicate that its global statistical strength and exact timing depend on the treatment of temporal variability. An objective change-point analysis identifies a marked decrease in seismicity centred on April 2015, nearly four years after storage operations began, and the decrease remains evident using a conservative magnitude threshold. Seismicity subsequently remains lower despite continued cyclic operations. The selected focal mechanisms show predominantly strike-slip to oblique source kinematics across pre-operational, operational, and post-operational periods. We interpret these observations as evidence for an evolving temporal and spatial association between storage operations and a pre-existing fault–reservoir system. 7ca96782ebe481ca: Topographic amplification is widely invoked to explain strong shaking and slope failure in mountainous terrain, yet direct field observations remain limited. In contrast, the NS slope exhibits a persistent narrow-band station-to-valley Fourier spectral-ratio peak at 3.5–4.0 Hz that remains stable across events and processing choices. Absolute spectra confirm enhanced energy at the slope in this band, while also showing that a relative spectral depression at the valley reference contributes to the large ratio magnitude. f5e310a0e62694b4: Gölbaşı (Adıyaman) Town, located within a basin along a left-stepping segment of the East Anatolian Fault Zone in Türkiye, experienced severe damage during the 6 February 2023 Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.6 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. 9bce4b078c1bfb8e: Transform faults contain rheological weaknesses that can be reactivated into either divergent or convergent boundaries, depending on tectonic stress regime. The East Sea (Japan Sea), a back-arc system at the junction of the Eurasian, Pacific, North American, and Philippine Sea plates, offers an ideal setting to understand this process. These results provide a kinematic framework linking the back-arc opening of the East Sea to its Late Cenozoic inversion, and document a rare example of transform-to-thrust reactivation in a continental back-arc setting.
c52198d1f33922c8: Fluid injection during reservoir stimulation aims to enhance reservoir permeability but induces seismic activity that persists for hours to months after injection has stopped. We evaluated several statistical models to represent the seismicity rate and the pressure decay. Using the best fitting model, we show that the time required to reach a given fraction of the initial seismicity rate and of the initial pressure are correlated, with the pressure relaxation being longer than the seismicity rate relaxation. No correlation is observed between seismicity decay and injection parameters such as injection volume, average injection pressure, or injection duration. These observations suggest that the relaxation of the pore pressure drives the decrease in seismicity, which has strong implications for reservoir management.
1b8565bccb4246d3: Forecasting the size of a future volcanic eruption in densely populated areas is a key aspect of volcanic hazard and risk assessment. We find that the EMG distribution provides a good statistical fit to both volcanoes' eruptive records, supporting the use of a power-law distribution for forecasting the volume of the next eruption.
aa9bb4e9ee4e2f30: The Olympos–Ossa region of mainland Greece preserves a high-pressure nappe sequence that exposes metamorphic equivalents of the Cycladic Blueschist Unit (CBU) in the Cyclades. Additionally, our age data affirm that the tectonic evolution of the Ambelakia Unit parallels that of the CBU passive margin sequence of the central Aegean, while the Olympos–Ossa Unit correlates with the Basal Unit in the Cyclades.
87f1da87a26ebf0b: Volcano deformation data provide important constraints on magma dynamics during volcanic unrest and eruptions. 1659adf9eca57103: During the night of 4–5 September 2026, residents of the Bandung area, 240–300 km from Anak Krakatau, reported repeated booms and rattling windows, while Jakarta, 150 km from the volcano, reported almost none. b964034f03d98977: We report the detection by the InSight seismometer of a long-period infrasound wave detected about 5.8 hr after the S1094b impact on Mars, on December 24th, 2021. e1c752027430d17a: The application of machine learning to planetary geophysics is frequently bottlenecked by a scarcity of labeled data and the complexity of non-stationary seismo-acoustic signals. The framework systematically extracts a feature vector using two novel pathways: (1) a Textural path that utilizes Hilbert space-filling curves to map 2D spectral patterns into 1D sequences for advanced information-theoretic analysis (e.g., permutation entropy, fractal dimension); and (2) a Spatial path driven by PDFSI (Probabilistic Distribution Fitting for Signal Identification), a novel probabilistic pre-conditioning engine that quantifies spatial connectivity by dynamically separating coherent signal modes from stochastic noise. Furthermore, application on the high data volume DAS dataset confirms its computational efficiency and domain-agnostic capability to isolate anomalous seismic arrivals from background noise. Ultimately, Spec2VEC bridges the interpretability of classical signal processing with the discriminative power of modern representation learning, providing a reliable, interpretable foundation for automated discovery across the geosciences. 3312d1ddb95f6998: The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, environmental, and infrastructural parameters, each assigned relative weights commensurate with its significance. Along the eastern coastal corridor, localities including Hammam Faraun, Ras Sudr, and Abu Zenima were identified as suitable for Flash Steam systems at drilling depths of 3,000–4,000 m, corresponding to reservoir temperatures of 140–210 °C, while Binary Cycle systems are applicable at depths of 2,000–3,000 m with temperatures ranging from 100 to 160 °C. On the western coast, sites encompassing Ras Gharib, Ras Shukeir, Jabal al-Zeit, and Jabal Ataqa are technically viable for Flash Steam technology at depths of 3,000–4,000 m and temperatures of 140–210 °C, with supplementary Binary Cycle suitability observed at depths of 2,000–3,000 m and temperatures of 100–180 °C. Zones exclusively suited for Binary Cycle applications include Ayoun Moussa, Wadi Baaba, Wadi Feiran, and Wadi El-Tor to the east, and Zaafarana, Wadi Dara, and Wadi Araba to the west, at depths of 3,000–4,000 m with temperatures ranging between 100 and 160 °C and 100–155 °C, respectively. ca1a7032ea888723: On January 26, 2026, an Ms5.5 shallow-focus earthquake occurred in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province. 60558c07ab74fec9: This is the Seissol parameters file for the study by Wong et al., Fitful but sustained rupture of the 2026 Mw 7.6 Venezuela earthquake. Updated on Oct 17, 2026. Please feel free to contact [email] for any questions.
c27824dbfe7d84c9: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. Implemented in our open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0, this formulation---combined with fewer, table-free and multithreaded spherical-harmonic transforms, improved file handling, and physics-inspired iteration starts---achieves an end-to-end speed-up of over three orders of magnitude (up to 4,000-fold) against the same 1-D GIA solver, reducing day-long simulations to under thirty seconds on a workstation. In particular, Numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided the AI agents' implementation choices and helped reject ineffective optimizations.
6879b3c464b3180a: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. 6ad77b2795a8d15a: Bayesian geophysical inversion provides a probabilistic framework to estimate subsurface properties, in which uncertainties are represented by a so-called posterior probability density function (pdf). Here, SMVI is first tested on two synthetic seismic inverse problems, demonstrating that SMVI can recover non-Gaussian, complex and multimodal posterior solutions accurately and efficiently. Then, we apply SMVI to real seismic data by performing Love wave tomography of the British Isles, and obtain inversion results that are consistent with previous Monte Carlo solutions. Around the East Irish Sea sedimentary basins, SMVI captures bimodal uncertainty associated with ambiguity in basin boundary locations, revealing alternative subsurface structures compatible with the observations. These results indicate that SMVI generalises various previous variational methods, and provides a practical and effective framework for quantifying complex uncertainties and supporting geological interpretation of seismic images.
b145bc15358b17ea: In geothermal systems, injected fluid flows along preferential fracture pathways and exchanges heat with matrix blocks. At fixed pressure difference, heating accelerates and broadens the front, whereas cooling delays and sharpens it. The terminal discharge depends only on the endpoint viscosity ratio, while matrix uptake, storage and contrast determine its approach time. At fixed rate, viscosity alters only the pressure drop, not the thermal response. Finite thickness controls the transition to capacity-limited equilibration, and strong matrix uptake collapses the isoviscous response onto a two-variable similarity surface.
c3c35a47d4cc38b4: Quartz is a dominant rock‐forming mineral in the continental crust and is expected to play a crucial role in affecting fault mechanics. Generally, the measured friction coefficients generally fall within the range of 0.55–0.70 and shows a double‐peak temperature profile. The rate‐ and state‐dependent friction (RSF) parameters, and , depend on both temperature () and velocity (). The slip behavior is characterized by pervasive v ‐weakening friction over specific ‐ranges at all the temperatures investigated. In the space, there are three domains dominated by unstable slip, corresponding to three low‐ regions. One domain falls at 300–550°C and 0.003–1 μm/s, suggesting plausible conditions for earthquake nucleation at depths, when extrapolated to natural faults. The low‐ T (v . Our results provide a detailed friction parameter map that facilitates analysis of earthquake nucleation and early acceleration processes.
f052019d0e934e57: Elastically accommodated grain‐boundary sliding (EAGBS) is a plausible source of upper‐mantle seismic attenuation and dispersion, yet classical theory predicts a localized Debye‐like peak that is absent or only weakly expressed in dry olivine experiments. 400852800749edde: Seismic attenuation in lunar lower mantle can provide critical constraints on thermal state and composition of the deep interior; however, previous estimates based on path-integrated amplitudes are strongly influenced by near-surface scattering, especially for narrow-band waveforms recorded by Apollo’s sparse seismic stations. Here, we show that the amplitude ratio between ScSH and SH from the same station can mitigate this limitation. We measure these ratios from narrow-band records and invert for lower-mantle Q by matching them with synthetic predictions that account for geometric spreading, source radiation and interface transmission. Synthetic tests verify that the method recovers Q within 10 % for signal-to-noise ratio ≥ 10 and remains robust to scattering and source mechanism uncertainties. Application to a terrestrial deep earthquake recovers Q = 308 (IQR: 280–340), consistent with the Preliminary Reference Earth Model (PREM) reference value (Q ≈ 312), confirming its feasibility on real data. Application to Apollo deep moonquake records (10 stacked records) shows that the amplitude ratios exhibit the expected single-peak distance trend and yield broadly consistent Q estimates across narrow bands, though the limited data warrant interpreting these results as a feasibility demonstration. This framework provides a practical and complementary constraint on lunar lower-mantle attenuation and is transferable to other planetary data sets with similar data limitations.
0ee7a1b9415271bd: The driving force of plate motion remains a central unsolved problem in solid Earth science. This study develops a conceptual, testable framework of lithosphere–asthenosphere coupling that asks whether the contrast in hydraulic stress transmission between the solid lithosphere and the partially molten asthenosphere can supply a distributed horizontal driving force for plate motion. The framework rests on two elementary mechanical premises: in a solid elastic medium under gravitational loading, the horizontal stress is approximately one-third of the vertical stress for a Poisson ratio near 0.25; whereas in a fluid or fluid-like medium, pressure is transmitted almost isotropically, so that the horizontal stress approaches the vertical stress. At an effective depth of about 70 km, the resulting horizontal normal stress contrast reaches the order of Pa. This paper quantitatively discusses two questions bearing on the physical plausibility of the mechanism. The first is the initial melt trigger: overpressure from closed-volume expansion driven by mantle thermal anomalies, reduction of the minimum principal stress by basal tensile stress, and stress concentration at pre-existing microstructures can act together to nucleate the first microfractures. The second is the mechanical feasibility of compressional offset at convergent boundaries: in a gravity field, the minimum principal stress is nearly vertical; when horizontal compression exceeds rock strength at a local weak surface, shear sliding on the fracture surface preferentially occurs along the vertical component, causing one plate front to move downward or overthrust. The model predicts a horizontal compressional stress of about 500–1500 MPa. This exceeds the critical buckling stress of the lithosphere, about 55–600 MPa, by factors of about 11–27; therefore, compressional offset and downward displacement are mechanically feasible. Trench formation requires a large, young, thin, and relatively uniform oceanic lithosphere, together with the dynamic condition of being “unable to move” or “blocked”; large-scale trenches do not form within continental lithosphere. These conditions are most easily satisfied beneath the thin lithosphere of the early Earth, which provides a quantitative mechanical basis for a multi-plate, small-scale, fast-cycling Archean tectonic style. The model further explains the evolution from discrete magmatic intrusions to linear rifting at mid-ocean ridges, the compressional-offset coupling between ridges and trenches at convergent boundaries, and the possibility that asthenospheric return flow is opposite to plate motion. From ridge to trench, the oceanic plate may gradually shrink rather than maintain a constant area. In the reference scenario, the global driving force is about N, and the mechanical power is about 11 TW; under conservative parameters, the estimates remain of order N and several TW. This study does not exclude a role for slab negative buoyancy, lithospheric cooling, or mantle convection in the present plate system. Rather, it proposes a possibly underestimated distributed pressure-transmission mechanism and sets out predictions that can be tested against seismic anisotropy, the thermal structure of subduction zones, and numerical modelling. The model is offered as a hypothesis with explicit falsification conditions and a well-defined scope. Its central inference can be refuted by a single class of observation: if global thermobarometric statistics for mantle xenoliths show that the pressure anomaly beneath mid-ocean ridges cannot be accounted for by the thermal expansion relation—that is, if a pressure deficit persists beyond the thermally induced density deficit—the model fails. Future work should give priority to the systematic compilation and joint inversion of the global xenolith thermobarometric database.
2b15c94e73d7915f: Seismic anisotropy provides a direct observational constraint on mantle flow in Earth's lowermost mantle. However, mineral fabric that generates anisotropy develops progressively and can preserve a memory of past deformation, rather than simply reflecting present-day flow. Here we investigate this memory by coupling 3-D global thermochemical convection models (with plate reconstruction consistent kinematic boundary conditions) since 230 Ma with mineral texture evolution while making forward predictions of the seismic signal. Models reproduce first-order present-day lower-mantle thermochemical structures, and piles with a relatively small intrinsic density excess and a high bulk modulus produce seismically observed edge morphologies of large low velocity provinces (LLVPs). The computations generate observed global patterns of D′′ anisotropy, including rapid variation of radial anisotropy across pile boundaries, with stronger anisotropy outside and generally weaker anisotropy inside the piles. At large scales, predicted fast polarization directions broadly follow present-day mantle flow, whereas regional departures reveal the influence of accumulated deformation history. Along the eastern margin of the African LLVP, calculations along observed SKS-SKKS ray paths reproduce key features of the regional splitting pattern, consistent with deformation associated with Tethyan subduction. The predicted anisotropy is sensitive to mineral rheology: Weakening associated with the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition localizes deformation near the core-mantle boundary and produces a strong depth dependence to the anisotropy, consistent with that observed beneath the western Pacific. Together, these results show that present-day seismic anisotropy records both the current mantle flow field and its geological history, providing constraints on long-term mantle dynamics and lowermost-mantle rheology.
82a41332bb1f1389: Understanding the temporal and spatial scales over which normal faults grow and interact is crucial for constraining seismic hazard in regions of active faulting such as Central Greece, where destructive earthquakes have been widely documented. In principle, subsurface and geomorphic datasets should provide complementary insights into fault evolution, allowing fault growth and interaction to be resolved across millennial to million-year timescales, a broader range than can be achieved using either method alone. However, the expression and evolution of normal faults in the subsurface and landscape have generally been explored independently of one another. We focus on the South Gulf of Evia active rift system in Central Greece, where several active normal faults bounding the southern rift margin have recently been mapped, including the Nea Palatia, Kalamos and Varnavas Faults. The availability of both geomorphic and seismic reflection data makes this an ideal natural laboratory to reconstruct their growth and evolution. We present new interpretations of vintage 2D seismic reflection data for the first time since their acquisition in the 1980s, including a new offshore age model for the eastern basin, which indicates that linkage of the two Varnavas Fault segments likely occurred between ca. 12–245 ka. These subsurface constraints are integrated with analyses of tectonic knickzones preserved in river long profiles, providing insights into early fault evolution over 10 5 –10 6 years. We propose fault initiation times for two end member bedrock erodibility scenarios for the Nea Palatia, Kalamos and Varnavas Faults. By applying a coupled landscape and basin analysis we reconstruct fault evolution from million-year to Holocene timescales and provide a proof of concept for the use of this integrated workflow to decipher the evolution of faults over contrasting and interconnected timescales in active rifts. Highlights A new offshore seismic-stratigraphic age model for the South Gulf of Evia Vintage 2D seismic reflection data reveals recent fault evolution over the past ca. 245 kyrs Fault initiation and early interaction recorded by river profiles over 10 5 -10 6 yr timescales Coupled landscape-basin approach resolves fault evolution over Holocene to million-year timescales
7985ab1ac223662f: The Pampean flat-slab subduction zone (29°–32°S) in the south-central Andes is characterized by a volcanic gap, strong crustal deformation, and a heterogeneous lithospheric mantle, yet the distribution of deformation and hydration remains incompletely resolved. Here we present the first regional 3D attenuation models of this system, derived from P- and S-wave spectra of local earthquakes using a transdimensional Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo tomography approach that quantifies model uncertainties. The resulting models reveal strong lateral variations in attenuation across both the crust and lithospheric mantle. In the continental crust, elevated attenuation is concentrated in the Precordillera and adjacent regions, spatially correlating with major tectonic boundaries and previously mapped fault systems, suggesting that small-scale heterogeneity and fracturing play a primary role. In contrast, lower attenuation in the eastern Sierras Pampeanas is consistent with comparatively less deformed crust. In the lithospheric mantle, attenuation patterns vary systematically along strike. Low attenuation in the western segment is consistent with a relatively cold and dry mantle, whereas higher attenuation above the flat slab may reflect increased hydration and/or the presence of fluids. Farther east, moderate attenuation is compatible with a more depleted and relatively dry lithosphere, while increased attenuation near the transition to steeper subduction may be associated with higher temperatures and possible partial melting in a re-established mantle wedge. Attenuation anomalies within the flat slab itself further suggest enhanced fracturing of the subducted Juan Fernández Ridge.
f95785d68ee4b399: Local magnitude (ML) must remain consistent as a seismic network combines surface and borehole installations and changes its recorded responses. It can also underestimate large earthquakes. We calibrate an ML scale for Taiwan from more than eight million Wood–Anderson amplitudes at 188,109 earthquakes and 873 stations, with a separate correction for every instrument and for every interval over which its response was unchanged. In calendar year validation experiments, estimating corrections while excluding the test year reduced the median dispersion among all station magnitudes by more than 50% and reduced the misfit to moment magnitude by 21%. We also derive an amplitude magnitude MA and adjust it for saturation, and the reported magnitude changes from ML to the adjusted value when MA exceeds 5.5. The adjustment improves agreement for the largest earthquakes of the calibration set, although they are few. The equations and three correction tables allow the scale to be applied across the calibrated network.
c34a1c1dcb52312c: Summary Magnetotellurics (MT) provides critical constraints on Earth’s electrical conductivity structure and thereby illuminates lithosphere and mantle processes. The EarthScope USArray MT program provides a unique opportunity to investigate large-scale tectonic and compositional variations across the contiguous United States (U.S.). However, uniform MT interpretation is hindered by data quality and the computational and initialization demands of 3D inversion. To provide a physically consistent and uncertainty-aware continental-scale baseline, we develop CURIE (continental U.S. 1D resistivity inference ensemble), comprising two complementary probabilistic reference model ensembles obtained by independently inverting the Zxy and Zyx components from 1773 MT stations using unsupervised, physics-driven normalizing flows. For each station and mode, CURIE provides posterior resistivity distributions, uncertainty estimates, and predicted MT responses. We assess the 1D assumption using filtered data misfit, mode differences, and phase tensor skew and ellipticity. Most stations yield filtered misfits below 4, indicating that 1D models reproduce the dominant responses. Low phase-tensor skew and ellipticity broadly coincide with low-misfit regions across the Interior Plains and the Intermontane Plateaus, whereas elevated indicators and misfits along tectonic and continental margins identify areas where 1D interpretation requires greater caution. At shallow depths, CURIE recovers resistivity patterns associated with major geological provinces; at mid- to lower-lithospheric depths, it resolves the broad contrast between the tectonically active western U.S. and the stable eastern craton. Differences between the Zxy and Zyx results along the Pacific and Gulf coasts, and in Florida further reflect orthogonal sensitivities to conductivity gradients and indicate 3D structural orientations, with some near-coast misfits influenced by the coast effect. The resulting dataset provides a continent-wide probabilistic reference that offers a first-order view of the U.S. electrical structure while supporting data quality assessment, identification of potential 3D effects, and development of initial or reference models for future 3D inversion and geodynamic interpretation.
f9259f03c791da39: Summary Seismic wave modeling and full-waveform inversion (FWI) are important tools for investigating subsurface structures and properties. Open-source seismic modeling and inversion tools enable researchers to test new methods, reproduce published results, and use waveform data to characterize the subsurface. However, building flexible FWI workflows still requires substantial effort to integrate wave solvers, misfit functions, and inversion algorithms. We introduce the Open Wave Library (OWL), an open-source framework that integrates these capabilities for local- to exploration-scale modeling and FWI. We implement high-order finite-difference solvers for 2D and 3D isotropic acoustic, isotropic elastic, and general anisotropic elastic media. We combine curvilinear meshes and local refinement to represent topographic elastic free surfaces, and use complex-frequency-shifted multi-axial perfectly matched layers to support stable simulations in strongly anisotropic media. For FWI, we implement conventional waveform, correlation, and adaptive waveform misfits to accommodate different waveform characteristics and degrees of cycle skipping. We also develop two objectives based on generalized dynamic time warping: one penalizes the estimated time shifts, while the other measures amplitude differences after warping. We regularize the time-shift estimates and use a common warping function across components for multi-component data. We compute adjoint-state gradients using source wavefields reconstructed from stored boundary values. We accelerate modeling and inversion through shot-level parallelism, distributed-memory domain decomposition for 3D models, and OpenMP shared-memory parallelism. We assess solver accuracy and numerical consistency through unit tests and comparisons with spectral-element solutions. Through sensitivity-kernel studies and synthetic and field data examples, we demonstrate the complementary behavior of the misfit functions and the applicability of OWL to heterogeneous, anisotropic, and topographic models. OWL assumes negligible Earth curvature and is not intended for regional- or global-scale simulations. Our current implementation runs on central processing units (CPUs); support for heterogeneous computing architectures, viscoelasticity, and coupled acoustic–elastic media remains for future development. With OWL, we provide an extensible platform for methodological research and reproducible seismic modeling and inversion.
856d25bba6fa971d: High-resolution airborne magnetic surveys are increasingly used to image shallow volcanic structures, but interpretation remains challenging in basaltic volcanoes where strongly magnetized lava, shallow intrusions, and hydrothermally altered rocks coexist beneath rugged topography. In such settings, conventional linear formulations can be unreliable because self-demagnetization modifies internal magnetization, and finite-element response evaluation may depend on the observation mesh. We develop a self-demagnetization-aware magnetic inversion framework based on a hybrid finite-element and volume-integral formulation. The finite-element solution resolves the susceptibility-dependent internal magnetic field, whereas the volume-integral operator evaluates the external magnetic anomaly from the resulting magnetization distribution at arbitrary airborne observation points. This separation avoids refinement around dense flight-line observations and suppresses mesh-dependent local-gradient artifacts. An analytical ellipsoid benchmark verifies that the formulation reproduces the response of a high-susceptibility body and provides stable sensitivities for inversion. Application to unmanned autonomous helicopter magnetic data from Izu-Oshima volcano reveals a heterogeneous susceptibility structure beneath the summit caldera. The recovered model images a shallow magnetic layer associated with recent volcanic products and a deeper low-susceptibility domain consistent with hydrothermal demagnetization. Around Mt. Mihara, the susceptibility distribution separates crater-fill lava, laterally distributed buried magnetic bodies, and demagnetized zones that cannot be resolved from the map-view magnetic anomaly alone. Comparison with existing electrical constraints supports a coupled shallow magmatic and hydrothermal system. These results show that self-demagnetization-aware inversion of high-resolution magnetic data can image lava accumulation, shallow magma emplacement, and alteration-related demagnetization in basaltic volcanic systems.
2188826b8c954358: This study presents shear wave splitting (SWS) estimates for core-refracted SK(K)S phases utilizing data from nine seismic stations in the Central Indian Tectonic Zone (CITZ) that were temporarily operational between July 2023 and July 2025. The CITZ was formed during the Mesoproterozoic orogeny in central India, resulting from the collision of the northern Bundelkhand Craton with a jumble of South Indian cratons. We used transverse energy minimization methodology to ascertain the SWS parameters, the fast polarization directions (FPDs) and splitting delay times ( δ t ). A total of 129 high-quality SWS measurements were obtained from 87 earthquakes ( M >5.5) at epicentral distances between 84–145° for SKS phases and 84–180° for SKKS phases. The mean δ t s at each seismic station ranges from 0.7 to 1.4 s, demonstrating the upper mantle heterogeneity in the study region. Most stations show NE-SW FPDs, aligning with the Absolute Plate Motion (APM) of the Indian plate. Ray-piercing-point spatial coherency analysis suggests that 200–250 km is a promising average depth of anisotropy, indicating that the primary source of the observed SWS measurement is mantle flow at asthenospheric depths, rather than frozen lithospheric fabric. The difference between mean FPD and APM direction at some stations suggests the presence of fossilized anisotropic fabrics resulting from prior orogenic events during the Mesoproterozoic Era. Seismic stations near the Deccan Volcanic Province and mantle dyke zones have lower δ t (
e68fe4c9500e9f26: The devastating 2026 Venezuela earthquake was cataloged as a doublet of \Mw~7.2 and 7.5 events. Combining NISAR and ALOS-2 Synthetic Aperture Radar data, teleseismic source imaging, and ensemble Kalman inversion of multiple moment tensors and dynamic rupture simulations, we show that the 2026 Venezuela earthquake was instead a single \Mw~7.6 event with variable rupture speed and seismic moment release. The earthquake rupture went through episodes of acceleration and deceleration, including a pronounced slow-down around the rupture area of the 1967 \Mw~6.6 Caracas earthquake. Stress transfer from the partially arrested front and a trailing slip pulse enabled the rupture to break through this stress barrier and release ~26% of the seismic moment beneath the coastal cities of Playa Grande and Caraballeda, where damage was most severe. Such fitful ruptures enhance high-frequency seismic radiation and challenge conventional methods for characterization of large earthquakes.
25d7928c58c81eb7: Least-squares reverse time migration (LSRTM) estimates a broadband reflectivity image by iteratively minimizing the data misfit. Despite its superior imaging performance over conventional reverse time migration (RTM), LSRTM is fundamentally limited by the first-order Born approximation and incurs a high computational cost due to the iterative solution of a source-dependent model-space Hessian. We propose dual RTM, a seismic imaging framework that reformulates the inverse problem in the dual space, where the optimization variable is the scattering information of all orders, rather than being limited to the first-order scattering of the Born approximation. Unlike LSRTM, which directly estimates the reflectivity model, dual RTM reconstructs the missing scattering data (dual variable) through a fixed-point iteration governed by the full wave equation, enabling the recovery of higher-order scattering and multiple reflections without repeated background velocity updates. Furthermore, dual RTM replaces the source-dependent model-space Hessian with a source-independent data-space Hessian. A hybrid time--frequency formulation enables this Hessian to be assembled and inverted once in the Fourier domain as an offline preprocessing step, reducing the online computational cost of each dual iteration to that of a single RTM application. Numerical experiments on challenging synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that dual RTM suppresses acquisition footprints, improves amplitude fidelity, and enhances deep imaging where primary reflections alone provide insufficient illumination. These results establish dual RTM as an efficient bridge between conventional RTM/LSRTM and nonlinear waveform inversion for high-resolution large-scale seismic imaging.
8af442f0a4faddbe: Purpose - Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study investigates the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a critical gap in the existing literature related to high computation times and energy costs of the simulations. Methodology - A numerical cryohydrogeological study on water and energy transfer in a forested, continuous permafrost site has been conducted using parallel high-performance computing to simulate the permafrost dynamics. The numerical results reasonably replicate the measured soil temperature profiles and the dynamics of infiltrated waters. This work uses a spectral network to achieve a fast, reliable, and stable surrogate model for the simulations to forecast over long periods of time. The surrogate is also enhanced by assimilating experimental data through the development of a hybrid modeling framework. Findings - The proposed approach improves the physical simulation while maintaining the stability of the dynamic model over long periods of time. The results reveal that the proposed hybrid modeling remains stable in integration and forecasting. The final hybrid solution demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation accuracy when tested against a test set of measurements. Predictions of the permafrost behavior in the coming decade are later made based on the CMIP6 climate change scenarios. Originality - This research offers a novel perspective on permafrost modeling that extends the current understanding of its behavior under different climate change scenarios. It shows a higher-than-expected temperature increase of the permafrost. Moreover, the stable forecasting of climate change effects is demonstrated.
e4154036b49cbddf: Seismic attenuation is a key indicator of crustal heterogeneity and energy dissipation, yet the physical mechanism of coda‐wave attenuation remains unclear due to the combined influence of scattering and intrinsic absorption. In this study, we analyze multi‐frequency S‐wave coda attenuation using the seismic recordings from USArray. Our results reveal that S‐wave coda attenuation exhibits pronounced frequency dependence, with distinct dominant mechanisms across different frequency bands. At lower frequencies (1.5 and 3 Hz), attenuation is primarily controlled by scattering associated with crustal heterogeneities and velocity contrasts, whereas at higher frequencies (6 and 12 Hz), intrinsic absorption becomes the dominant mechanism and exhibits a strong correlation with surface heat flow, consistent with temperature‐dependent viscoelastic dissipation. Comparisons with attenuation models derived from other seismic phases highlight their different sensitivities to depth and frequency, indicating that no single approach can fully capture the complexity of attenuation. These findings underscore the diagnostic value of multi‐frequency coda‐wave attenuation and highlight the importance of integrating various attenuation measurement methods to better constrain crustal heterogeneity and thermal state, with implications for improved crustal imaging and geodynamic interpretation.
f2c61e648e22cf26: Geodetic and seismic observations before the 2011 M w 9.0 Tohoku‐oki earthquake indicate decadal‐scale acceleration of aseismic slip along the northern Japan Trench, but the mechanism remains debated. We show that this transient can be explained by creep‐front propagation that progressively erodes heterogeneously locked asperities. We invert GNSS velocity fields from 1998 to 2009 using a mechanically motivated model in which locked regions are confined to historical rupture areas while their effective sizes and process‐zone stressing rates evolve. The models fit both velocity fields and predict slip accelerations consistent with repeating‐earthquake estimates. Inferred asperities occupied about 66% of their corresponding rupture areas in 1998 and about 37% in 2009, indicating substantial expansion of aseismic creep over the decade before rupture. The inferred shrinkage rates are consistent with fracture‐mechanics predictions for plausible coseismic stress drops. These results suggest that megathrust locking can evolve substantially over decadal timescales.
817f492183f6b1b9: Three-dimensional P-wave velocity (Vp) and Vp/Vs ratio models of Mauna Loa and Kilauea volcanoes, Island of Hawaii, from local earthquake tomography, as published in Lin et al. (2014), J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth, 119, 4377-4392, doi:10.1002/2013JB010820. Files: Lin2014_Hawaii_Vp.txt (columns: Lon, Lat, Dep, Vp in km/s), Lin2014_Hawaii_VpVs.txt (columns: Lon, Lat, Dep, Vp/Vs), and Lin2014_Hawaii_Vp_VpVs.csv (both models in one comma-separated table for easy import into GIS software). See README.txt for details. Grid: longitude -156.11 to -154.76, latitude 18.87 to 20.31 (decimal degrees), 3 km horizontal node spacing (48 x 54 nodes per layer), and 10 depth layers at -1, 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 20, 25, and 35 km (negative depth is above sea level), for 25,920 nodes in total. Nodes with poor ray coverage (e.g., model edges, offshore areas, and the deepest layers) remain at or near the starting 1D model and should not be interpreted. Please refer to the resolution tests in the paper, and cite the paper if you use the model. Funding for this research was provided by the National Science Foundation grant EAR-1246935.
23e69472af759086: The Sea of Japan coastal areas have experienced tsunami damage caused by submarine active seismic faults. Large uncertainties remain regarding seismic activity of these faults and the following tsunami. Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment (PTRA) enables the evaluation of tsunami risk accounting for such uncertainties. In this study, the tsunami risks of a thermal power plant located in Joetsu on the Sea of Japan coast were evaluated using PTRA based on submarine active faults, including coupled faults, across the Sea of Japan. The results indicate that coupled fault models had large impacts on risk levels, especially for severe damage states. For the most severe damage state, the median expected annual probability of experiencing this damage state among the structures increased by 154% when coupled fault models were considered. In addition, the risk levels varied depending on the structures, even within the same site. The spatial distribution of tsunami risk revealed that structures with high risk levels existed not only along the coast but also inland. The findings of this study provide practical insights into reliable tsunami risk assessment, which are useful for the development of disaster resilience measures, especially for infrastructure.
54bdece69605b169: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
5bdd83aa83ecf63e: Glacial Isostatic Adjustment (GIA) models solve the gravitationally self-consistent sea-level equation for the response of the solid Earth and the oceans to changing ice loads. As these models are increasingly embedded in coupled ice-sheet simulations, glacial-cycle calculations, and large ensembles, standard pseudo-spectral 1-D solvers face a steep computational barrier: they evaluate the viscoelastic response by explicitly re-summing every past load increment, scaling quadratically with time steps as $O(N^2)$. Here we show that this computational penalty is an artifact of algorithmic formulation rather than Earth physics. By exploiting the exponential form of the viscoelastic relaxation kernel, we reformulate the viscous response as an exact recursive update of a finite set of modal states, without re-summing the load history. This exact reformulation alone reduces the cost of a run to $O(N)$, yielding a 20.6-fold speed-up relative to a standard full-history 1-D GIA solver for a case study involving a 550-step Antarctic future sea-level projection. Implemented in our open-source solver SLEvolve v1.0, this formulation---combined with fewer, table-free and multithreaded spherical-harmonic transforms, improved file handling, and physics-inspired iteration starts---achieves an end-to-end speed-up of over three orders of magnitude (up to 4,000-fold) against the same 1-D GIA solver, reducing day-long simulations to under thirty seconds on a workstation. Beyond this solid-Earth application, SLEvolve illustrates how human-derived analytical reformulations can be combined with benchmark-harnessed AI-assisted engineering to modernize scientific software. In particular, Numerical regression tests and performance profiling guided the AI agents' implementation choices and helped reject ineffective optimizations.
ebb3837bb814f60a: Bayesian geophysical inversion provides a probabilistic framework to estimate subsurface properties, in which uncertainties are represented by a so-called posterior probability density function (pdf). Estimating this pdf is computationally challenging when it is high dimensional or complex, particularly if it may be multimodal. We introduce Stein mixture variational inference (SMVI) for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion with multimodal or complex posterior solutions. The method combines parametric variational inference with Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD). In SMVI, the posterior pdf is approximated by a mixture (sum) of distributions, in which component distributions are optimised jointly using the SVGD update rule. This construction combines computational efficiency with the flexibility to represent a range of plausible Earth models and allows components to be updated in parallel. Here, SMVI is first tested on two synthetic seismic inverse problems, demonstrating that SMVI can recover non-Gaussian, complex and multimodal posterior solutions accurately and efficiently. Then, we apply SMVI to real seismic data by performing Love wave tomography of the British Isles, and obtain inversion results that are consistent with previous Monte Carlo solutions. Around the East Irish Sea sedimentary basins, SMVI captures bimodal uncertainty associated with ambiguity in basin boundary locations, revealing alternative subsurface structures compatible with the observations. These results indicate that SMVI generalises various previous variational methods, and provides a practical and effective framework for quantifying complex uncertainties and supporting geological interpretation of seismic images.
cb449e1cf1f5ddad: Three profiles of wide-angle seismic traveltime data offshore Oregon are analyzed to determine two-dimensional compressional-wave velocity structure. Tomographic imaging of the Juan de Fuca (JdF) plate reveals a porous, hydrated upper crust and a dry lower crust and uppermost mantle. The accretionary prism is imaged as a wedge of lower-velocity material oceanward of Siletzia, a high-velocity block in the upper plate. Seismic velocity boundaries within the prism align with previously identified kinematic discontinuities, including the static backstop of Siletzia and the transition between active (oceanward) and non-active (landward) wedge deformation. As the JdF plate interacts with and subducts beneath Siletzia in Central Oregon, the JdF crust fractures and releases pore water into the overlying wedge by 12-15 km depth, as evidenced by coincident localized velocity reductions in the slab and wedge and the seafloor seeps. Dewatering along this 100-km segment leaves the JdF plate generally dry as it enters the mantle. Localized slow-velocity anomalies suggest locally increased hydration, potentially consistent with evidence for water input farther down-dip in the subduction system.
7841ba7ff0002328: Finite-fault attributes, such as rupture elongation in buried earthquakes, may reflect the spatial organization of fault stress and strength. We quantify rupture elongation using rupture aspect ratio (RAR), derived from the spatial second seismic moment of slip for 51 screened finitefault models spanning 𝑀𝑤 4.45–7.43 whose ruptures neither reach the surface nor span the seismogenic thickness. Observed RARs range from 1.02 to 1.59, with a median of 1.18 and a pronounced upper tail toward elongated ruptures. We then use three-dimensional boundaryintegral dynamic rupture simulations to determine how heterogeneous fault properties modify rupture geometry. Homogeneous self-arresting models reproduce the nearly circular RAR range but fail to reach the most elongated ruptures. Introducing directional heterogeneity in initial stress and frictional properties broadens the simulated RAR distributions and generates substantially greater elongation. Across the tested parameter ranges, initial-stress amplitude and directional structure exert the strongest influence on RAR. Several heterogeneous parameter combinations are compatible with the observed high-RAR subset, showing that similar rupture geometries can arise from different fault states. The RAR distribution therefore provides a statistical, rather than deterministic, constraint on classes of directionally structured fault states. Together, the observations and simulations establish a quantitative framework for evaluating candidate directional organizations of fault stress and strength from the RAR statistics of buried ruptures.
7c49dbee64426597: Interseismic locking on the Main Himalayan Thrust (MHT) governs where crustal strain and seismic moment accumulate, yet published locking inversions vary substantially with assumptions about fault boundary and coupling kinematics. We combine Himalayan Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) measurements with a viscoelastic earthquake-cycle model that includes interseismic viscous flow in the lower crust and mantle and an approximation for gradual migration of the locked−creeping boundary on the MHT. We invert baseline length-change rates and evaluate 20 model configurations that vary fault-block kinematics and lower-crustal and mantle viscosity structure. Across the ensemble, strong locking is concentrated above mid-crustal ramp segments, whereas uncertainty peaks near ramp transitions and along the downdip edge of locking. Increasing lower-crustal and mantle viscosity shifts the inferred locked zone farther downdip. Inferred strongly negative process zone stressing rates along the bottom boundary of locking across much of the margin suggest up-dip propagation of creep into the locked zone. A stationary end-member with zero process zone stressing rate fits the data more poorly and distributes moment accumulation broadly across the interface from the surface to ∼45 km depth, producing a gradual transition from locking to full creep. In contrast, the nonstationary solutions concentrate nearly all moment accumulation within the locked zone and exhibit a rapid transition to full creep outside it, yielding locked-zone moment accumulation rates roughly twice those inferred from the stationary model. These results refine Himalayan moment-budget estimates and highlight how rheology and boundary dynamics influence geodetic coupling inferences.
7970e2155f8f0e20: Constraining the crust beneath Campi Flegrei is critical for understanding its magmatic system, but the resolution of local-earthquake tomography decreases with depth. Here, we adapt receiver-function analysis to intermediate- and deep-focus earthquakes within the Ionian slab beneath the Tyrrhenian Sea, recorded by the dense Campi Flegrei seismic network at regional distances. Deep sources provide steep P-wave incidence, while relatively short source–receiver paths reduce high-frequency attenuation receiver functions are corrected for finite-distance moveout and modelled using ray-theory simulations and global optimization. Synthetic tests assess the resolution of the method. The preferred model identifies a prominent interface at 7.7±0.4 km depth, associated with a low-velocity, high- layer, and a deeper discontinuity at 21.7±0.9 km, interpreted as the Moho. The 7.7 km interface is consistent with the top of the magmatic sill identified by the 2001 active-source experiment. No additional shallow discontinuity is required by the data within the resolution of the method.
d9640b38d8c6c70d: Rapid and accurate hypocenter determination based on three-dimensional (3D) seismic velocity models is essential for seismic monitoring in subduction zones, yet it remains computationally demanding. HypoNet Nankai, a hypocenter determination package that uses physics-informed neural network (PINN) travel-time inference for a realistic 3D P-wave velocity model of the Nankai Trough subduction zone, was designed to address this problem, but supported only P-wave arrival times. Here, we present HypoNet Nankai PS, which extends the framework to both P- and S-wave travel times. We first constructed an S-wave velocity model from the existing P-wave model using empirical conversion relations for marine sediments and the crust. Because the resulting S-wave velocity structure has lower velocities and therefore considerably steeper travel-time gradients, the original PINN training procedure designed for the P-wave velocity structure was insufficient. We therefore revised the training procedure by reconsidering the distribution of collocation points, the NN architecture, and the optimizer. Benchmark comparisons with the fast marching method showed that the revised approach substantially reduced the root-mean-square deviations for both P- and S-waves compared with the original algorithm. Recovery tests using synthetic earthquakes were also performed. When applied to 223 earthquakes recorded by DONET stations off the Kii Peninsula, the system yielded hypocenters generally consistent with the JMA catalog beneath the network, suggesting that the 3D velocity model captures travel-time variations accommodated by JMA's 1D model and station corrections. Farther seaward, the estimated hypocenters were substantially shallower than those in the JMA catalog and were located in the oceanic crust and uppermost mantle, consistent with previous relocations that used DONET data and 3D velocity models.
7dfb4f06f23ead8a: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known. We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation. The critical temperature increases with pressure, from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa, and we find no phase separation at 3000 and 4000 K up to 100 GPa. The slope of the critical curve decreases substantially between 0.3 and 30 GPa, and the curve nearly flattens above about 30 GPa and 2000 K, where molecules begin to give way to atomic species. The coexistence curves are asymmetric with an ammonia-rich critical composition. For the expected envelope compositions, the phase boundary lies close to, and intersects, published thermal profiles of Uranus and Neptune, implying ammonia may be raining out in these planets today. In contrast, in warm sub-Neptunes such as TOI-270 d, ammonia and hydrogen are likely miscible in all proportions. Together with previous studies, our results suggest that silicates, water and ammonia separate from hydrogen in sequence as planets cool, with implications for their compositional, thermal and structural evolution.
0d314d71949fe6b5: High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. These keels have probably been formed early in Earth’s history, and the preservation of these deep, cold, and highly viscous roots in a convective mantle remains enigmatic. A classical view is that the excess density due to colder temperatures is compensated for by a light composition. Here, we map the magnesium number (Mg#, a proxi for mantle depletion) within cratonic keels, based on the thermochemical interpretation of a global shear velocity model. Our interpretation suggests that depletion is strong above 150 km (Mg#>92), and decreases with depth down to the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary (LAB). However, changing only the major element composition and the Mg# does not fully meet the requirements implied by seismology or gravity observations. We explore various hypotheses, varying the temperature of the lithosphere, considering the presence of eclogite, accounting for chromium or for a minute quantity of diamonds. We also discuss the uncertainties in seismological observations of velocity and radial anisotropy as well as in mineralogical models. Changes in temperature, the presence of eclogite, of Cr incorporated in garnet, or radial anisotropy are inconsistent with shear velocity and gravity constraints when considered individually. Below the graphite/diamond transition, the combination of depletion with a low volume fraction of diamond ( 180 Ma) through the subduction of organic carbon.
cea04812ca1ef26b: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful tool for high-resolution subsurface imaging, but its practical use is limited by cycle skipping, strong sensitivity to the initial velocity model, and high computational cost. This study proposed a Fourier-enhanced dynamics FWI (FED-FWI) framework that combined three components within a recurrent neural network formulation of the forward problem. First, Fourier feature mapping was applied to the coordinate inputs of the multilayer perceptron (MLP) that parameterized the velocity model, which enriched the neural tangent kernel spectrum and improved the representation of sharp velocity contrasts. Second, a composite misfit coupled an optimal transport term, which was robust to phase shifts, with a wavelet-domain term that enforced multiscale consistency; the two terms were adaptively balanced by exponential moving average weighting according to their smoothed relative magnitudes, and the resulting coefficient was not required to vary monotonically with iterations. Third, an optimizer that modulated the update magnitude according to the cosine similarity between successive gradients suppressed oscillatory updates and stabilized convergence. The framework was implemented with automatic differentiation, so the adjoint equations need not be derived manually. Starting from a linear initial model that spanned 1200–4800 m/s, without prescribing a known, fixed velocity for the shallow water layer in the initial model, FED-FWI recovered the Marmousi II model with a structural similarity index of 0.804 and a mean squared error of 0.075, compared with 0.626 and 0.212 for optimal transport FWI and 0.695 and 0.134 for Sobolev-norm FWI; it also attained the shortest convergence time of the methods compared while requiring less than 200 MiB of additional graphics processing unit memory. Ablation tests indicated that each component contributed to this improvement, and two salt-model experiments showed that the principal salt geometry was recovered under strong velocity contrasts. The results indicated that FED-FWI improved inversion quality when initialized with the linear velocity model considered in this study.
968ac429d8bc0f8c: Detecting tsunamis in the open ocean before they reach the coast is critical for saving lives, yet open-ocean observations remain sparse and costly. Submarine telecommunication cables span many tsunami-prone regions and can be instrumented with distributed sensing, but their tsunami sensitivity remains uncertain. Here we report observations of the transoceanic tsunami generated by the Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake on 29 July 2025, obtained through distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) on a 400-km telecommunication cable array offshore Chile. After suppressing background and instrumental noise, we recover coherent tsunami signals along hundreds of kilometres of cable despite maximum open-ocean amplitudes of only ~ 4 cm. The recovered signals agree with tsunami simulations, while revealing spatial variability in cable sensitivity. Converting DAS strain to water elevation empirically, we reconstruct the tsunami wavefield and predict coastal tide-gauge records where constrained by high-fidelity cable segments, providing 5 to 15 minutes of warning time before the tsunami arrives at the coast. These results demonstrate the viability of an end-to-end tsunami warning system based on existing submarine cables.
b0532e43e1b3c66b: Following the September 2021 M S 6.0 Luxian earthquake in China's Luzhou shale-gas field, soil methane enrichment shifted between fault zones and the epicentral area. We combine 4 surveys during 2021–2026 with 2021 isotopes, seismicity, shallow geophysical structure, and mechanical calculations to examine this redistribution. Concentration–carbon-isotope covariation (ρ = 0.61; n = 14) supports a thermogenic contribution compatible with regional shale gas. Enrichment was concentrated on the anticlinal flanks in 2021, weakened in 2023, peaked centrally in 2024, and shifted northwestward in 2026. Localized buried slip and heterogeneous Coulomb stress changes favor selective adjustment of existing pathways. We interpret the sequence as rapid shallow release, episodic deeper replenishment, and a later northwestern response associated with local seismicity. Methane thus provides a geochemical tracer of evolving subsurface connectivity, guiding monitoring of fossil methane escape after strong earthquakes.
a505cac4ec15f524: The 7 January 2025 Mw 7.1 Tingri earthquake ruptured the southern Xainza–Dinggye rift in the Tibetan Plateau, ∼200 km north of the Himalayan frontal thrust system. This rift lies in a network of discrete normal and strike-slip faults that accommodate gravitational collapse and lateral extrusion of the Plateau with overall India–Eurasia convergence. Subpixel image correlation and coseismically shifted digital elevation model differencing of high-resolution (∼0.5 m) satellite optical imagery reveal the full 3D coseismic displacement field of the earthquake. Rupture occurred on two west-dipping faults: the Lagoi fault in the north, cutting through mountainous terrain at relatively high elevation (∼5500 m) within granitic–gneissic rocks, and the Dingmu Co fault in the south, bounding a lower elevation (∼4200 m) basin within Tethyan metasedimentary rocks. Northern deformation consists of coherent, block-like oblique hanging wall subsidence with left-lateral slip (>2 m). Southern deformation is more distributed, with comparable magnitudes of subsidence and northwestward translation accommodated along a series of hanging wall faults. Footwall rebound is minimal and occurs over shorter distances than observed in the long-term landscape record. Between these domains, a ∼5–10 km wide east–west transition zone absorbs diffuse north–south contraction (∼1 m) and right-lateral motion (∼1.5 m), above a concave-up along-strike curved fault imaged by aftershocks that may direct slip toward its deepest center. Collectively, these observations indicate the control of topographic stresses, lithology, fault geometry, and a weak lower crust in partitioning discrete and diffuse deformation during a single earthquake, reproducing Plateau-wide kinematic patterns typically inferred from geodetic and geomorphic observations over much longer timescales.
fcd6a01f93172d3b: Characterizing the physical properties of frozen lakes, such as ice thickness and water depth, is essential for diverse applications, including ice safety assessment and climate change monitoring. Typically, these properties are measured through labor-intensive field surveys, limiting their spatial and temporal coverage. Alternatively, frozen lake environments can be investigated using seismology. Seismic waves propagating on floating ice travel at velocities that depend on physical properties of the ice–water system, including the elastic properties and thickness of the ice and the water depth. Because seismic waves are frequently generated and can propagate through entire lake systems, they have greater spatiotemporal coverage than field measurements. In this study, we investigate the use of wind-generated flexural waves recorded by a distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) system to infer ice thickness and water depth along a 1000 m fiber-optic cable installed on Lake Pääjärvi, southern Finland. We detect flexural waves in the 0.01–0.5 Hz frequency band, measure their phase-velocity dispersion curves, estimate ice thickness and water depth along four cable intervals, and compare the estimates with field measurements and the lake bathymetry. The ice-thickness estimates are comparable to field measurements, with differences ranging from 2% to 34%, whereas the water-depth estimates underestimate bathymetry values by 22%–60% while resolving the increasing water-depth trend along the cable. We find that water-depth estimates tend to become less robust as the water depth increases because the measured dispersion curves lack sufficiently low wavenumbers to resolve the water column. We illustrate that flexural waves can refract toward the shore as they approach shallow water. This effect must be considered when estimating true phase velocities from apparent velocities measured along the cable to avoid bias in the estimated ice thickness and water depth. Our results demonstrate the potential of DAS to leverage ambient signals for monitoring frozen lakes.
fc9a89719f3de107: We deployed 500 seismic nodes across 257 locations at Cape Modern, Utah, over several months to characterize temporal velocity variations in the shallow subsurface using ambient-noise tomography. Because of the nature of ambient noise and minor changes in the sensor locations, the available ray paths were modified during the acquisition. A Voronoi tessellation-based path resampling strategy mitigated azimuthal bias from heterogeneous station distributions, achieving quasi-uniform ray-path coverage. Spatial mapping of velocity changes reveals lateral heterogeneity in the evolution of relative velocity change (dv/v), with velocity perturbations varying across the study domain and spatial patterns reflecting underlying variations in material properties and subsurface structure. Analysis of continuous data systematically reveals dv/v decreases followed by gradual recovery, with frequency dependence (0.5–1.2 s) indicating a shallow subsurface origin. Integration with environmental monitoring identified thermoelastic forcing as the dominant mechanism, with calculated velocity change variation matching observations (0.6% for 25°C seasonal variation). The 90–100-day delay between air temperature and velocity response aligns with thermal diffusion timescales. At shorter periods (0.5–0.8 s), high-velocity regions showed rapid recovery (60–95 days), whereas low-velocity zones exhibited extended recovery (90–130 days), reflecting thermal conductivity differences. The absence of systematic correlation at longer periods (0.8–1.2 s) indicates thermal decoupling of deeper intervals. This study demonstrates the monitoring capability of a dense array for spatially resolving heterogeneous subsurface thermoelastic responses.
210b88a2659b8440: On 6 February 2023, an earthquake doublet occurred in the East Anatolian fault zone (EAFZ), producing significant surface displacements and causing extensive damage in Türkiye and Syria. The EAFZ is known to be spatially complex, with multiple segments, fault stepovers, and fault-bend structures. How such fault complexities modulate the co- and postseismic distribution of fault slip remains an important question. We use Sentinel-1 and Advanced Land Observation Satellite-2 Synthetic Aperture Radar-derived pixel offset measurements and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) static offsets for the two events to constrain the distribution of coseismic slip along both strands of the EAFZ. We constrain the postseismic slip distribution using Sentinel-1 interferograms and GNSS time series. We adopt a Bayesian framework to explore the solution space, relying solely on physically justifiable prior information without employing artificial regularization. We account for both observational errors and epistemic uncertainties due to imperfect knowledge of the regional elastic structure and orientation of the fault plane. We find that elastic afterslip mostly surrounds the areas of coseismic rupture. However, the geodetic data sets that span the postseismic period cannot be explained solely by elastic afterslip. We also confirm the potential seismic gap on the boundary between the Erkenek and Pütürge faults, across which neither coseismic nor postseismic slip occurs in the periods considered here.
94df5031882351ee: New earthquake forecasting models are increasingly reported to outperform established models such as the epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model. However, the scientific meaning of such improvements depends critically on how the benchmark is constructed. I use the term “under-implemented ETAS” for a benchmark that is unnecessarily restricted, weakly optimized, or otherwise disadvantaged, and propose the Parity of information, Optimization, Generality, and Assessment (POGA) test as a simple framework for assessing model comparisons. The purpose is not to protect ETAS from competition, but to ensure that improvements over established models are scientifically interpretable. A strong benchmark makes victory harder, but also reveals what a new model has genuinely learned that its competitor could not.
5831f19b3f2a414c: In seismic source inversion using teleseismic P waves, P-wave arrival times are picked from observed waveforms and used to adjust their timing relative to the predicted arrivals. However, uncertainty in the picked arrival times remains after this correction. Picking errors shift the entire waveform and produce temporally correlated waveform errors. If these errors are not properly accounted for, small differences in arrival-time picks may substantially alter the inferred source models and contribute to discrepancies among analysts. In this study, I propose a waveform-shift covariance approach that approximately constructs the component of the data covariance matrix associated with P-wave picking uncertainty from observed waveforms and a probability distribution of time shifts. I incorporate this approach into potency density tensor inversion (PDTI) and compare it with a conventional approach that neglects picking uncertainty, using 125 synthetic waveform datasets that differ only in picking errors. Relative to the conventional approach, the proposed method reduces the normalized model root mean square error (RMSE) by approximately 0.09 and reduces the variability among inferred source models across datasets to less than 40% of that for the conventional approach. Although the normalized data RMSE is comparable between the two approaches, the normalized model RMSE for individual datasets is concentrated within 0.32–0.36 for the proposed method, whereas it spans 0.35–0.50 for the conventional approach. These results show that incorporating P-wave picking uncertainty into the data covariance matrix yields more accurate and stable source models, even though the proposed and conventional approaches fit the observed waveforms similarly well. Application to real earthquake data with uncertain P-wave picks suggests that neglecting the data error structure may lead to overfitting in the conventional approach. Accounting for picking uncertainty changes how waveform discrepancies are weighted in the inversion, reducing the tendency to interpret waveform-shift errors as source complexity. These findings underscore the importance of returning to a basic principle for reliable estimation of earthquake rupture processes: interpreting source signals in observed data requires an understanding of not only the signal structure but also the error structure.
868f749162e2f6b0: Different geophysical processes generate characteristic seismic waveforms. Identifying similar waveforms therefore helps to distinguish between different source mechanisms and to monitor seismic activity in settings ranging from volcanoes and glaciers to urban environments. In many applications, however, the seismic event types are unknown and no labelled training data is available. Then, unsupervised clustering is necessary. Most existing approaches require all input vectors to have the same length, which in seismology translates to a fixed event window. However, seismic signals can differ considerably in duration: This may require events to be cropped or padded to a common length, which may lead to a loss of important waveform characteristics. Furthermore, the approaches commonly rely on extensive feature engineering or machine-learned representations, which often require hyperparameter tuning and can reduce the physical interpretability of the resulting clusters. In addition, many clustering algorithms require the number of clusters to be specified a priori, limiting their flexibility when analysing previously unknown datasets.
