This study introduces Incrementally Buffered Dynamic Time Warping Clustering, a new unsupervised clustering algorithm that operates directly on seismic time-series data using a small number of physically interpretable parameters. The method is based on Dynamic Time Warping and is particularly suited to noisy and continuously active seismic environments, where overlapping signals and imperfect event catalogues are common. The buffered and incremental structure of the algorithm explicitly identifies outliers and allows new clusters to form during incremental updates, enabling continuous monitoring without reclustering the entire dataset. The algorithm is evaluated on a labelled volcano-seismic dataset, where it achieves a clustering accuracy of 69.39 per cent, comparable to previously published supervised approaches. A second application to Antarctic icequake data demonstrates its ability to identify meaningful waveform groups in a setting with limited prior knowledge of event types. These results show that the newly introduced clustering algorithm provides an interpretable and scalable framework for clustering large seismic datasets while retaining direct access to waveform similarity in the time domain.
3d886425d68758bb: The Carboneras Fault Zone (CFZ) is one of the most active structures of the Alborán Sea, and together with the Al-Idrissi Fault, forms part of the Trans-Alborán Shear Zone (TASZ), which accommodates ongoing Africa-Eurasia convergence. Despite its tectonic significance, the offshore geometry and segmentation of the CFZ remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate multibeam bathymetry, high-resolution multichannel seismic reflection data, and three-dimensional (3D) structural modelling to reassess its offshore architecture. Our results show that the offshore CFZ forms a deformation corridor exceeding 110 km in length, comprising five principal and seven subsidiary fault segments. Individual segments range from 6.48 to 41.1 km in length and strike between N46º; and N79º. Interpretation of nine stratigraphic horizons, from the Tortonian acoustic basement to the seafloor, enabled the reconstruction of a 3D geological model of the fault system. Along-strike variations in deformation style, uplift, and segmentation allow subdivision of the CFZ into northeastern, central, and southwestern sectors. Structural complexity is greatest in the central sector, where fault branching, pressure ridges, a sag pond, and flower structures define a deformation corridor up to 4.1 km wide, and where uplift and accommodation contrasts between structural highs and fault-controlled depocentres are strongest. This complexity coincides with the transition between the dominant NE-SW-striking segments (N46º-N59º) and the more easterly southwestern segments (~N79º). Our findings refine previous models by resolving the 3D geometry, segmentation, and along-strike variability of the offshore CFZ, providing new insights into fault localization, tectonic inheritance, tectono-sedimentary evolution, and constraints for seismic-hazard assessment.
50781a9b7e8262f0: A deep earthquake swarm has continued beneath northern Yamaguchi, southwestern Japan, near the Abu Monogenetic Volcano Group since February 2025. We investigated its spatiotemporal evolution and source processes using hypocenter relocation and moment-tensor analysis. Relocated hypocenters are concentrated at depths of approximately 25-35 km and exhibit distinct geometries evolving with time, including inclined planar structures in the south and a relatively horizontal structure in the north. Several episodes show diffusion-like hypocenter migration, with apparent diffusivities of 0.12-4.57 m 2 /s. Moment-tensor solutions are diverse and include significant non-double-couple components, while locally clustered events often show similar or nearly reversed mechanisms. These observations suggest that fluid-pressure perturbations associated with deep fluids propagated through a pre-existing heterogeneous fracture network, sequentially reactivating locally favorable structures. The swarm highlights transient deep fluid related seismicity near the Moho beneath a region without recent surface volcanism.
13fef29a0d915003: The propagation of seismic waves through the Earth’s mantle is controlled by the dynamic response of the mantle to oscillating stresses and strains. This dynamic response arises from the elastic, anelastic and plastic properties of the minerals and rocks in the mantle and can vary with the amplitude and frequency of strain oscillations. Previous experiments at pressures of the lower mantle have either determined the elastic properties of minerals and mineral aggregates at much higher frequencies than those of seismic waves or have focused on their plastic deformation under static stresses. Here, we present cyclic loading experiments that probe the dynamic response of magnesium oxide (MgO) powder at pressures of the lower mantle and at frequencies that extend into the range of seismic frequencies. MgO powder was compressed in a diamond anvil cell and subjected to loading cycles generated by a piezoelectric actuator. During loading cycles with varying strain amplitudes and frequencies between 10 and 100 millihertz, we collected X-ray diffraction patterns in radial diffraction geometry and at a rate of one pattern per second. We analysed the resulting time-series of diffraction patterns by extracting lattice spacings from the reflections 200 and 220 of MgO to derive volume strains and differential lattice strains from both reflections. While the oscillating components of volume strains reflect the isotropic compressibility of MgO, the oscillating differential lattice strains reveal a more complex response to cyclic loading that varies with the amplitude of strain oscillations. For larger strain amplitudes, we resolve phase shifts between the oscillating differential lattice strains of both reflections that indicate significant dissipation of strain energy by anisotropic plastic or anelastic deformation. At the smallest amplitudes of strain oscillations, the dynamic response of the textured MgO powder is described by almost uniform oscillating lattice strains consistent with elastic isostrain and minor dissipation. By following our experimental procedure, future cyclic loading experiments may characterize the dynamic response of polycrystalline materials at high pressures and quantify how dissipation of strain energy affects the seismic properties of materials in the Earth’s mantle.
5b40f2128c814dd3: Tsunami hazard severity — especially tsunami inundation depth — is related to the tsunami’s source mechanism. Traditionally, homogeneous earthquake rupture sources have been used as the source mechanism for tsunamis generated in the Cascadia Subduction Zone for regional hazard assessment. We show with 200 heterogeneous earthquake rupture sources how tsunami inundation hazards change for three sites located along the Cascadia Subduction Zone when the assumption of homogeneous slip is relaxed. Our results indicate that the tsunami inundation limit extends further inland compared to homogeneous sources. We also note that the 1-in-2475-year exceedance threshold extends further inland for heterogeneous earthquake rupture sources compared to official tsunami evacuation lines and the American Society of Civil Engineers tsunami design zone.
4a00970b73bdafc9: Periodic gravitational forcing by the Moon and Sun produces small oscillations in Earth's rotation known as nutations. Nutations are amplified by a resonance with a natural motion of the liquid core called the Free Core Nutation, whose amplitude is limited by friction‐like processes at the core–mantle boundary. Previous studies have attributed this damping to the dissipation of electric currents induced in the lower conducting mantle, but, given current knowledge of the lower mantle, electromagnetic coupling appears insufficient to fully account for the observed lag. We show that additional dissipation arises from the interaction of the tidal flow inside the core with the topography of the core–mantle boundary, which excites internal waves that extract energy and momentum from the flow. Adapting a theory originally developed for tides over seafloor topography, we find that the observed damping can be fully accounted for by a topography of typical amplitude ∼5 km dominated by features of wavelength ∼1,500 km. The dissipation is highest when the upper core is neutrally buoyant. Such amplitudes are larger than typical inferences from global seismic studies but are not ruled out, given regional seismic evidence for kilometer‐scale features and the sparse constraints at these scales.
b99c9a57268b46c9: Earthquakes affect surrounding fault systems through multiple mechanisms. Here, we examine a rare cessation of activity in 27 families of low‐frequency earthquakes (LFEs) that likely reflect fault creep at the southern edge of Cascadia subduction, near the Mendocino triple junction. These sources usually exhibit nearly daily activity but were shut off for ∼7–25 days following the December 2024 moment magnitude ( M w ) 7.0 Mendocino fault earthquake. Based on modeling, we infer that this cessation was not caused by induced shear stress, which was slightly encouraging of slip, but rather by combined clamping normal stress and reduced pore pressure. This mechanism, which isn't captured in the common effective friction simplification, may have strengthened the fault and inhibited creep, without requiring fluid outflow. Observed variations in LFE cessation times are not predicted by modeled stress changes alone and may instead reflect differing source dimensions or subtle variations in LFE fault geometry.
dbd385b03cd277ae: On January 30, 2025, an M4.7 earthquake shook the Eagle Ford Shale, Texas, the region's second M4 event in under eighteen months. Unlike much of the central United States, where induced seismicity stems from wastewater disposal, most of the earthquakes in the Eagle Ford are linked to hydraulic fracturing (HF) (Fasola et al., 2019; Fasola & Brudzinski, 2023). If HF-induced, the 2025 event would be the largest such earthquake in the United States, amid seismicity increasing in both magnitude and frequency. The seismicity appears to be associated with mapped normal faults in the Karnes Trough Fault Zone (KTFZ), but its detailed pattern and relationship to HF operations remain poorly characterized. This study leverages ~5 years of continuous TexNet recordings (~25 km station spacing) to better detect and locate this seismicity. We have developed a workflow (TM2DD) that integrates multistation template matching with automated per-template correlation thresholds, refines phase arrivals via template-detection cross correlation, and applies double-difference relocation using a local 1-D velocity model. This expands the detected catalog by 17.5-fold, with relocations revealing that the 2023 M4.0 and 2025 M4.7 sequences ruptured adjacent fault segments with 15-20 degree differences in dip angle. In addition, the larger event occurred at the deeper extent of the seismically active zone. All detected sequences correlate tightly in space and time with active HF wells within 3.5 km, with the deeper 2025 event showcasing mainshock - aftershock behaviour, whereas the shallower 2023 sequence is swarm-like. These results indicate that HF-induced seismicity in the KTFZ can propagate along adjacent, connected fault systems as nearby operations continue, with deeper segments potentially hosting larger, mainshock-dominated ruptures.
90e0371369480bac: A static arrest length and a fully dynamic rupture are compared, one rupture at a time, for 60 antiplane and 60 in-plane cases on one 120 km fault with linear slip weakening and one correlation length of the initial stress. The standard deviations were fixed before those ruptures were drawn. The comparison tests the rule, used to build earthquake populations, that a rupture stops where its static energy release rate falls below the fracture energy and that this rule decides which ruptures span the fault. In 22 of the 120 cases the two calculations disagreed on whether the rupture spanned the fault, and in all 22 the static criterion predicted arrest while the dynamic rupture spanned the fault. All 22 still spanned the fault when the spacing along strike was halved. Where both stopped, the dynamic length was longer in 41 of 42 antiplane cases and 38 of 40 in-plane cases, and the median ratio was 1.08 in each mode. The in-plane values depend on the grid across the fault: with half the nodes, the in-plane median ratio was 0.99 and seven of the twelve in-plane disagreements remained. Three-dimensional rupture and other slip-weakening distances were not tested.
edc71639885cf5d7: La Soufri'ere de Guadeloupe is an active volcano of the Lesser Antilles Volcanic Arc. Its last eruption halted in 1977, yet hydrothermal activity has increased over recent years, raising summit instability hazards. The link between hydrothermal fluids and detachment landslide surfaces is well established and exacerbated by inflation, pressurization, and fluid flow lubrication. Nodal Ambient Noise Tomography offers the resolution and penetration needed to investigate such features in 3D. In 2023, we deployed 39 nodal geophones that recorded for about 1 month. The resulting 3D S‐wave velocity model resolves a central low‐velocity conduit, possible flank detachment planes, and subsurface structures of the shallow volcanic cone. Our results highlight the complex interaction between fluid transport (meteoric and magmatic) and tectono‐magmatic drivers. This provides the first high‐resolution 3D seismic imaging for slope stability assessment in volcanic environments. Understanding detachment zone geometry and distribution contributes to hazard risk assessment and mitigation.
8031ff53e447ad22: Microseismicity in the Central Arctic remains understudied due to its remoteness from land stations. Hydrophone arrays can be used to detect earthquakes from their T-phases, components that propagate in water. This approach can provide a valuable alternative to traditional recording systems and improve the monitoring coverage. However, manual annotations of T-phases are a time-consuming process, and more automatic approaches are needed. Recent studies in T-phase detection consider machine learning techniques, but these methods are computationally intensive and sensitive to training data. In this study, an automated detector is presented utilising a Regions Of Interest (ROI) algorithm on spectrograms, requiring minimal parameter tuning and computational resources. The detector was applied to acoustic data recorded along the Nansen Basin from September 2019 to August 2020 during the CAATEX experiment. The ROI detector correctly identified 82 out of 96 manually labelled events across all moorings, with the majority of false detections linked to the presence of flow noise within hydrophones. The algorithm also characterised spectro-temporal properties of T-phase signals, with energy focused between 3 and 50 Hz, peaking at around 20 Hz. This method is robust against the varying underwater background noise conditions encountered and aids in studying the complexities of the T-phase signal structure.
d6d2cd3b94306f57: Landslide hazard is the probability of occurrence of an event of a given magnitude in a specific area and time period. The failure mechanism of the mass, and displacement needed to transition the hillslope from metastable to failure are fundamental inputs for coseismic landslide hazard analyses. In closely-jointed rock mass, joint-step-path failure mechanisms evolve with increasing rock-mass displacement. Three main stages have been hypothesized; incipient, transitional and avalanching. Investigating and characterizing these failure-stage transitions is critical for quantifying coseismic landslide hazard as the hillslope-specific scale. However, little is known about the magnitudes of rock mass displacement associated with these transitions. This study aims to quantify the hillslope displacement magnitudes required to transition a rock mass to failure. These thresholds are based on remote sensing measurements of displacement and derived estimates of normalised translational slope displacement (TSDs) - used as a proxy for rock mass deformation or strain - for six coseismic landslides situated in closely-jointed greywacke. Our results show that for a rock mass to transition from metastable to failure - the rock avalanche stage - requires TSDs greater than 5%, where the amount of TSD required varies with the hillslope angle. We propose an empirically-derived “translational slope deformation index” (TSDI); a function of the translational angle of displacement and normalised displacement along it. This novel tool could provide the link between the permanent slope displacements estimated using analytical methods, to the likelihood that a slope will transition into a more mobile, hazardous rock avalanche, during earthquake shaking.
24feb66ed1acff27: Summary Over the past few decades, InSAR and GNSS have significantly improved the monitoring of volcanic and tectonic processes by providing frequent, high-resolution measurements over large areas. To track magma transport and better understand the seismic cycle, these data are typically analyzed using kinematic solutions that model fractures as dislocations within an elastic, homogeneous half-space. Such simplifying assumptions can lead to inaccuracies when estimating the location and strength of subsurface sources. To address these limitations and determine more physically meaningful quantities - such as stress vectors rather than dislocations - we propose a new method for inferring variable pressure or traction changes on fractures, through the inversion of noisy InSAR or GNSS ground displacement data. These fractures may represent faults or magma intrusions embedded in a three-dimensional, heterogeneous crust with prominent topography. Our approach is based on a fictitious domain method inspired by the extended finite element method (XFEM), which is particularly well-suited for modeling fractures that need not conform to volume meshes. The inversion framework minimizes a cost function comprising the misfit between modeled and observed displacements, along with two regularization terms applied to both the tractions and their gradients. We present an inversion algorithm based on the forward and adjoint problem. The method is reformulated for InSAR data, which is challenging due to missing data, measurement noise, and the projection of displacements into Earth-satellite line-of-sight (LOS) directions, resulting in an incomplete displacement field. A corresponding adaptation for GNSS data is also introduced. Synthetic tests demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method even with a single LOS observation, or in the presence of spatial gaps and noise, as well as with few GNSS data. They show that, neglecting heterogeneities in the inversion may bias the distribution of pressure and their amplitude. Regularization parameters are determined using either L-curve analysis or a compromise function, both providing reliable results. We confirm that log-log L-curves, and not lin-lin L-curves, are required for appropriate regularization selection. As source depth or noise levels increase, the method favors stronger regularization, yielding smoother solutions. We apply the method to the May 2016 intrusion and eruption at Piton de la Fournaise, where InSAR and GNSS data are available for the beginning and end of the intrusion and eruption. Using a homogeneous elastic medium, the results agree well with those from a previous boundary element study, that assumed a homogeneous medium and pressurization over a circular portion of a dike. Inversion results for a heterogeneous elastic medium show greater complexity in the pressure distribution within the dike, but remain consistent with our previous findings. Furthermore, by inverting traction changes rather than pressure changes, we identify a shear displacement at depth–interpreted as a flank slip occurring simultaneously with the magma intrusion.
9cba63bdf5eab686: Understanding the complex subsurface structures of volcanic regions is crucial for hazard assessment and resource management. Traditional active seismic studies are normally limited for the exploration of shallower crustal structures using low-energy sources located at the Earth surface. While, using earthquake data, the deep seismic interfaces of the crustal structure can be imaged with high-energy and in-depth located sources. Here we propose a data simulating-processing-migration workflow for imaging the subsurface shallow crustal structure by earthquake synthetic signals. As a reference test-site for our study we used the Campi Flegrei caldera internal structure. Thanks to accurate earthquake locations now available in this area, we treat passive data like active data and employ advanced seismic imaging methods. For methodological assessment and improvement, we simulate 400 microearthquakes randomly distributed between 1 and 3 km depth in a vertically layered velocity structure and recorded by 13 stations. Exploiting the cylindrical symmetry of the vertically layered velocity model, we construct representative 2-D seismic sections by sorting synthetic source–receiver records as a function of source–receiver distance. This provides a controlled framework for identifying the different seismic phases and relating them to their corresponding reflecting interfaces prior to migration. Finally, we apply a modified Kirchhoff migration technique combining the Shifted Total Variation regularization and Principal Component Analysis to reconstruct images of subsurface structures. This workflow suppresses migration artefacts, enhances coherent events and extracts structural features that remain stable under model perturbations and noise contamination. The resulting images reliably recover major subsurface interfaces and provide a coherent and robust characterization of the subsurface structure.
88412cc6b812d05b: Summary Polarization observables have long been used to infer properties of the Earth, but the geophysical literature has not explicitly addressed the problem of a general metric for comparing arbitrary polarization states (independently of specific application contexts). To address this question, we first introduce a geometrical representation of polarization based on the Poincaré sphere. This framework allows us to derive a novel polarization discrepancy criterion, defined as the geodesic length between two polarization states represented on the Poincaré sphere. We establish, both analytically and geometrically, the relationship between this intrinsic metric and the main classes of polarization metrics (based on polarization angles, ratios and cross-products). Then, we examine the advantages and limitations of various polarization-based misfit functions from both fundamental and geophysical perspectives. On the fundamental side, we theoretically compare the different misfit functions in light of a few qualitative criteria. From a geophysical perspective, we extend the conventional multicomponent FWI method for inverting the discussed polarization-based criteria. With a simple numerical experiment, we show that misfit functions based on intrinsic and extrinsic distances (PoincarÃ© and normalised cross-product misfit functions, respectively) produce superior inversion results compared to all other polarization-based misfit functions. More generally, inverting polarization observables with a suitable metric can be beneficial for a wide range of geophysical problems, from source estimation to the quantitative imaging of Earth properties based on different types of physical fields (such as seismic or electromagnetic waves).
fde7882b18447632: Predicting the response of Antarctic ice to climate change requires detailed knowledge of its shallow structure, but direct measurements are challenging. Traditional seismic surveys are logistically demanding, and surface remote sensing provides limited information about subsurface layers. Here, we introduce uncontacted airborne seismology, a method that uses aircraft‐generated sounds and their conversion into seismic waves at the ice surface to probe the ice interior. Using a 36‐node seismic array during airborne passes, we captured multiple types of seismic waves and analyzed their propagation to extract dispersion patterns. Joint inversion of these observations reconstructs the elastic properties and porosity of the upper ∼100 m. This approach offers a rapid, scalable framework for mapping near‐surface ice structure and establishes a benchmark for future aerial or robotic exploration of polar regions, opening new possibilities for large‐scale, noninvasive monitoring of ice sheet dynamics.
b765018a4e0ff19e: Large language models (LLMs) can drive scientific software through function calling, but free-form tool use is fragile on long, data-dependent processing chains. Models omit arguments, invent units, feed the previous artifact into the wrong input, and report completion without a verifiable product. We present GeoAgent, an agent system for seismic data processing built on Madagascar's roughly 1{,}965 command-line programs. GeoAgent exposes 54 operator agents (51 generated from a declarative specification), retrieves from an index of 1{,}937 operators, and encodes the processing flow as a nine-stage state graph. Four explicit contracts---named artifacts, input resolution, parameter takeover, and artifact validation---move everything the graph can determine out of the model's discretion. A deterministic geometry tool parses the self-describing SPS/RPS/XPS and SEG-Y headers, cross-checks eight consistency conditions, and reproduces the reference shell recipe exactly. The system runs in containers with session- and task-level isolation, bounded execution, and defenses against silent failures. On a 2-D land dataset, the nine-stage pipeline completes in about six to eleven minutes and yields a verified artifact at every stage, while retrieval reduces per-turn tool context from about 12k to 2k tokens. We report the design, deployment experience, and motivating failure modes.
78ebb13a5601d68f: Frequency-domain wavefield modeling underpins seismic imaging and inversion, where repeated Helmholtz solutions become costly as velocity models, source locations, and frequencies vary. Neural operators learn mappings between physical fields, and their accuracy can decline outside the training distribution. Diffusion models learn wavefield distributions and generally require repeated sampling evaluations to produce accurate fields. A conditional mean flows model is introduced for complex scattered-wavefield generation. The analytical background wavefield serves as a condition alongside the velocity model, supplying spatially organized information about the source location and frequency. Learning the scattered wavefield avoids the point-source singularity in the target and supports generalization across these physical conditions. The model estimates the average transport velocity over a finite interval connecting Gaussian noise to the scattered field. This representation captures the accumulated displacement and permits both full-interval one-step generation and interval-partitioned sampling. Trained on OpenFWI, the model is evaluated on in-distribution and out-of-distribution velocity structures, frequency generalization, and inference efficiency. In most evaluated settings, one-step mean flows sampling achieves lower wavefield error than multi-step diffusion. Because each sampling step requires another network evaluation, accurate one-step generation also reduces inference time. These results indicate that mean flows can provide accurate and efficient frequency-domain scattered-wavefield generation.
b4533b09c515954c: Hotspot swells provide key constraints for understanding plume‐lithosphere interaction. However, quantitative relationships between plume properties and swell morphology remain poorly constrained. Here, we use 3D regional geodynamic models with composite diffusion‐dislocation creep rheology to investigate plume‐lithosphere interaction for intraplate hotspots. Model results show that plume material spreads beneath the lithosphere, forming a pancake that is modulated by non‐Newtonian rheology in the asthenosphere. Plume material spreads downstream notably more rapidly than plate motion, deflating the swell. Based on the modeled swell geometry, we derive two sets of empirical scaling laws linking surface dynamic topography to mantle plume properties. A simplified set relates swell height, width, and cross‐sectional area to plume buoyancy flux and plate velocity, while a second, more comprehensive set links swell geometrical metrics to plume radius, excess temperature, and plate velocity. Applying these scalings to observations for the Hawai'ian swell yields plume surface buoyancy fluxes well exceeding 4.2 Mg/s. The latter scaling yields either a narrower and hotter (297 km wide, excess temperature of 348 K) or a wider and cooler plume (447 km, 162 K), corresponding to plume surface buoyancy fluxes of 5.1 ∼ 5.6 Mg/s. Pure diffusion‐creep test models demonstrate that composite rheology systematically modifies swell geometry and its dependence on plate velocity, underscoring the relevance of our new scaling. Although melting‐related compositional buoyancy is not explicitly considered in our simplified models, these scalings provide improved quantitative links between surface dynamic topography and deep mantle plume properties.
215686b00dee6eee: Salt structures typically form due to the post-depositional flow of salt driven by differential loading, gravity gliding, or shortening, with the internal architecture of the evaporite treated as a passive strain marker. Using ~26,000 km² of 3-D seismic reflection data and 34 wells from the Southern North Sea, we show that the earliest regional deformation of the Southern Permian Basin salt giant (Zechstein Supergroup) was instead autogenic. The synclines of the first salt-cored folds overlie ridges of intrasalt gypsum that converted to anhydrite at the end of the Lopingian. Triassic onlap and truncation show that these folds formed immediately after salt deposition, long before Paleogene–Neogene shortening, and their curvilinear, unoriented pattern follows neither the sub-salt fault grid nor the dip of the detachment, as allogenic mechanisms would predict. Numerical experiments show that the density contrast created by the conversion suffices to make the ridges founder into the underlying halite, depressing the depositional surface above them into lows that Triassic sediments then filled. A significant component of Southern Permian Basin salt tectonics may therefore be autogenic in origin, with the distribution of the related structures being fixed by depositional mounding and diagenetic reactions within the evaporite rather than by regional, plate-driven stresses. Regional tectonism subsequently amplified these structures, which nonetheless retain the distribution imposed within the evaporite.
bea33b5253ee3ef5: This study involved an analysis of seismic data acquired in the surrounding area of the Belarusian Antarctic research station “Mount Vechernyaya” in February, 2023 to identify a possible relationship between the seismic noises and local meteorological parameters. Probability density functions of power spectral densities histograms were constructed using the ObsPy framework based on the source seismograms. Separate power spectral densities were also extracted for each time window for the more detailed analysis. In addition to the main peak of the secondary microseisms, some noticeable peaks can be identified in the range of 0.5-1.0 Hz on individual spectral power density graphs at certain time intervals. These peaks can be attributed to the so-called high-frequency microseisms that are often due to the coastal zone waves. The intensity of these peaks shows a significant correlation with the northward wind speed projection, with the correlation coefficient reaching its maximum at a time shift of 14 hours and can reach 0.51 for the horizontal components and 0.45 for the vertical component. The conducted polarization analysis shows the dominance of Rayleigh waves in the wave pattern of oscillations in the range of 0.5-1.0 Hz.
fd4c844ab2cc3f06: The faults in the Eastern San Francisco Bay Area in California have long been known as a source of seismic hazard. This potential for large earthquakes, paired with high population density and economic activity leads to high seismic risk in the Bay Area. In this study we utilize the physics-based earthquake simulator RSQSim to generate synthetic earthquake catalogs for the San Francisco East Bay. We run a suite of models with different fault connectivity and on-fault parameters. We compare the model catalogs with UCERF3 probabilities and paleoseismic data. We find that initial on-fault assumptions of friction, weakening and connectivity shape the resultant catalogs. Firstly, we find that all our catalogs have b-values greater than 1, with models with uniform velocity-weakening and strong coseismic weakening having the lowest b-values (~1.4). The b-values are higher (1.5~1.8) for models with velocity-neutral and velocity-strengthening patches. However, if only fitting Mw 5 and greater, all model b-values fall within ~1.0-1.2. Secondly, we observe connected faults leading to more multi-segment slip events for the Hayward and Calaveras faults. We also observe good agreement between the RSQSim models and the UCERF3 Time-Independent and Time-Dependent probabilities of Mw 6.7 or greater events on the Hayward and Calaveras faults, within the maximum and minimum probability bounds. Models without velocity-strengthening yield time-independent 30-year probabilities of 22.4-28.9% for the Hayward and 13.3-20.5% for the Calaveras and time-dependent probabilities of 17.3-42.2% and 12.5-25.3% respectively. Finally, we compare model results to the mean recurrence intervals at three paleoseismic sites using a Welch’s t-test. For all but three models (all of which have uniform velocity-weakening friction) we can reject the equality of the mean recurrence rate between the paleoseismic data at Tyson Lagoon and the model catalog at the 95% confidence level, motivating future work exploring the full spectrum of fault slip.
c5a377f0ebc65a4a: On 14 August 2021, the southern peninsula of Haiti was struck by an M w 7.2 earthquake that killed more than 2,200 people. The 2021 epicenter is located 95 km west of the M w 7.0 2010 Haiti earthquake and 7 km north of the main, geomorphic trace of the EW‐striking, left‐lateral strike‐slip Enriquillo‐Plantain Garden fault zone (EPGFZ) that forms a transpressional plate boundary between the Caribbean plate and the Gonâve microplate. Using a compilation of earthquake focal mechanism solutions, aftershocks, interferograms and coseismic displacements from ALOS‐2 and Sentinel‐1 Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), we propose that the 2021 earthquake ruptured a 2.5‐km wide band of steeply north‐dipping, secondary faults that bypassed the geomorphic prominent and curved 60‐km long restraining‐releasing paired bend on the EPGFZ. The initiating sub‐event of the 2021 mainshock is a left‐lateral and oblique thrusting event; that was followed by a left‐lateral westward‐propagating strike‐slip sub‐event along the proposed 65°N–77° N‐dipping Ravine du Sud bypass fault zone. We test our hypothesis by comparing two finite fault models that are constrained by the InSAR and global navigation satellite system displacements both on and off the bypassed restraining‐releasing paired bend on EPGFZ. We then compare our proposed model for fault evolution of the EPGFZ with similar examples of strike‐slip fault systems at a variety of map scales that are characterized by the same type of fault‐straightening process as we propose here for the 2021 Haiti earthquake.
5569188baaffa83f: The northwestern margin of the South China Sea experienced complex continental breakup, yet the specific lithospheric stretching modes and degree of crustal thinning in the Xisha area remain highly debated. Specifically, determining whether the Xisha trough is underlain by relatively thick or hyper‐extended continental crust is crucial for understanding the region's deep thermal structure and passive margin geodynamics. To address this, we employed a 2D multi‐observable modeling approach (LitMod2D). By jointly fitting free‐air and Bouguer gravity anomalies, geoid height, topography, and surface heat flow, while incorporating seismic reflection and refraction constraints, we constructed a robust lithospheric thermo‐chemical structure model for the region. Our results reveal significant lateral heterogeneity in the depth of the lithosphere‐asthenosphere boundary (LAB). The LAB beneath the Xisha block is comparatively deep and laterally uniform, occurring at depths of ∼90 km. In contrast, the LAB beneath the surrounding troughs and oceanic basins is significantly shallower, rising to depths of 50–70 km. Modeling results indicate that the Xisha trough is underlain by hyper‐extended continental crust (∼4–6 km thick), consistent with regional high heat flow anomalies and observed tectonic patterns. This indicates that thermo‐tectonic processes play a controlling role in lithospheric stretching and evolution. Synthesis shows that lithospheric extension in this region is consistent with predictions of the depth‐dependent stretching mechanism. Stretching strain is mainly concentrated in the upper crust and uppermost mantle, whereas the rheologically weaker middle and lower crust undergoes plastic flow, acting as a slip layer that buffers overall lithospheric deformation.
a7850fd4de628365: The Xiaojiang Fault (XJF) forms the eastern boundary of the Sichuan‐Yunnan rhombic block. Although its central and northern segments have hosted M ≥ 7 earthquakes along the main trace, large earthquakes near the southern segment mainly occurred on the intersecting Qujiang Fault (QJF) and Shiping‐Jianshui Fault. The structural controls on this deformation transfer remain unclear. We investigated the QJF‐XJF junction using continuous ambient‐noise records from 229 short‐period stations deployed in 2023. Rayleigh‐ and Love‐wave dispersion measurements were directly inverted for 3‐D S‐wave velocity and azimuthal anisotropy to 6 km depth. Shallow velocity variations broadly follow surface geological units. A pronounced velocity gradient across the QJF reflects lithological contrasts, whereas a low‐velocity zone along the western branch of the southern XJF likely indicates fracture damage and material weakening. Integrated with GPS velocities and geomorphological evidence, the anisotropy pattern indicates segmented shallow deformation: the western XJF branch appears relatively less active, whereas the QJF plays a more dominant role in accommodating regional deformation. The 1970 Ms 7.7 Tonghai earthquake source region contains an upper‐crustal high‐velocity anomaly adjacent to a sharp velocity‐gradient zone. We infer that the distributed geometry and weakened materials of the southern XJF disperse deformation among multiple branches, whereas the greater structural continuity of the QJF and strong cross‐fault structural contrast favor elastic‐strain accumulation and larger ruptures. Our results constrain shallow strain transfer from the southern XJF to intersecting faults and its role in large‐earthquake nucleation and rupture.
34be5e645306152d: After more than 2 years of quiescence following its major 2018 flank lava effusion and summit caldera collapse, Kīlauea, Hawaiʻi, returned to frequent eruptive activity in late 2020. Microgravity measurements from the summit region in 2019 and 2022 span this reawakening and indicate a gravity increase of up to hundreds of microgals near the center of the summit caldera. Much of this increase is caused by lava that partially filled the 2018 collapse pit. We accounted for this mass by differencing digital elevation models of the summit area to determine the geometry and amount of accumulated lava and its gravity contribution at each station in the network. The remaining gravity change is best approximated by a mass increase of 6.9 × 10 10 kg (5.1–23.0 × 10 10 kg at 95% credible interval) at a depth of 480 m (121–795 m at 95% credible interval) beneath the locus of the 2018 collapse. The modeled source depth reflects the combined impacts of magma accumulation in a reservoir known from previous geophysical studies to exist at about 1–2 km depth, intrusions between that reservoir and the surface, and mass accumulation in the heavily fractured caldera floor. The spatial and temporal patterns of subsurface mass accumulation during 2019–2022 imply that there were no significant changes in magma reservoir geometry or magma supply to the volcano in the years following the 2018 collapse.
c82f2b907be31dc8: Summary Emerging sensing technologies across the physical sciences and engineering, including arrays of many sensors, have revolutionized the ability to collect high-resolution, large-scale datasets continuously. Although these advances have opened up new possibilities for scientific discovery, public data archives of some communities struggle to accommodate the sheer volume of larger datasets, and research teams face growing difficulties in efficiently exploring, transferring, visualizing, and interpreting the data at scale. These challenges are particularly pressing in the geophysics and seismology communities, which have encountered data that are several orders of magnitude larger in recent years. Array coherence, which relies on the similarity between sensor pairs within an array to analyze coherent signals, is effective in enhancing the detection of weak or emergent signals in noisy environments. In this study, we show how array coherence can be leveraged to effectively manage a surplus of data and serve as a robust method for signal detection and identification of regions of interest for further analysis. We present a novel algorithm that employs a QR decomposition to efficiently approximate array coherence and enhance the time resolution of detected signals, providing more precise signal detection. We demonstrate the utility and efficiency of this algorithm on data from a continuously recording, dense seismic array, allowing us to identify candidate seismic events and reduce the amount of data that require further transfer and analysis.
28270f8fe5e9cb38: Aseismic slip plays an important role in the earthquake cycle. On oceanic transform faults (OTFs), the majority of fault slip occurs aseismically which makes OTFs a natural laboratory to study the physical mechanism of aseismic slip and its interaction with seismic rupture. In this study, we apply state-of-the-art methods to analyze the aftershock sequences of three Mw > 6.5 earthquakes on the Mendocino OTF offshore California, including the 1994 and 2024 Mw 7.0 earthquakes, which are one of the largest OTF earthquakes so far. Compared with similar-magnitude continental strike-slip earthquakes, these large Mendocino OTF earthquakes have an order of magnitude fewer aftershocks, suggesting limited inter-event stress triggering. Nevertheless, their aftershock zones expanded with logarithmic time substantially beyond the co-seismic rupture zones, likely reflecting propagating aseismic slip transients. This behavior suggests that low-seismic-coupling segments can host aseismic slip transients triggered by earthquakes in neighboring high-seismic coupling segments while limiting the propagation of these seismic ruptures. In addition, the aftershocks of the 1994 and 2024 Mw 7.0 events, together with abundant background seismicity and previously identified repeating earthquakes, surround the rupture zones of the 2024 Mw 7.0 event and a Mw 6.1 earthquake in 2021, which suggests heterogeneous embedding of seismic slip patches within a predominantly aseismic slip zone in the eastern Mendocino OTF. Our observations reveal heterogeneous slip behavior and complex interaction between seismic and aseismic slips along the Mendocino OTF possibly due to variation in fault zone serpentinization and/or fluid-filled porosity.
93cd141e0dbecddd: This study introduces a new dimensionless index, the Basin Sloshing Index (BSI), to provide a unified explanation for long-period ground motion and persistent shaking observed in large sedimentary basins. Inspired by fluid sloshing dynamics, BSI is defined using three fundamental parameters—the basin scale L, seismic wavelength λ, and attenuation factor Q —and takes the simplified form: BSI=2πQ(L/λ) Applying representative values for the Kanto Basin yields BSI ≈ 12,500 (≈10⁴), indicating an extremely high level of inertial dominance comparable to strongly resonant fluid sloshing systems. This high BSI naturally explains key features of long-period ground motion in the Kanto Basin, including amplification in the 5–10 s band, double peaks, prolonged shaking exceeding 100 s, and sensitivity to distant earthquakes, all of which arise as consequences of dynamic flattening. Using the analogy of cake batter in a baking pan (BSI ≈ 12,500), the study illustrates that solid Earth behaves fluid-like in the long-period regime, enabling intuitive understanding of basin-scale resonance. Furthermore, dynamic flattening induced by repeated deep large earthquakes may have contributed to maintaining the anomalously flat geomorphology of the Kanto Basin for over one million years, a process that can be quantitatively interpreted through BSI. Finally, the free oscillation of the Earth following great earthquakes—characterized by BSI ≈ 2,500—is shown to lie on the same dimensionless “worldline” as basin-scale sloshing, suggesting that BSI provides a unified framework applicable continuously from basin-scale dynamics to whole-Earth oscillations.
5a52b4867b1718fa: Near-surface velocity structure plays a crucial role in modulating ground motion, and, in turn, contributes to seismic risk. However, a complete understanding of the basin effect is limited, owing to the paucity of detailed shallow basin structure, geological structures and near-field seismic sources. In this study, we perform physics-based simulations of ground motions incorporating the sedimentary low-shear velocity layers in the Wellington basin to evaluate the fundamental characteristics of regional seismic responses. We simulate ground motions of frequency up to ~2 Hz for intermediate-size earthquakes around Wellington, then validate acceleration time series and spectral amplitude ratio against GeoNet strong motion records. After that, we simulate potential dynamic ruptures of Mw> 7 earthquakes on the Wellington Fault, investigating the impact of rupture directivity effects on basin amplification. Our models demonstrate distinct ground intensity patterns arising from dynamic fault ruptures, rather than from distant seismic point sources, revealing significant spatial variation in basin amplification.
5f41e181681bd0cd: Fault zone heterogeneity takes several forms, such as surface roughness, lithological variations, and the intermixing of mineral phases with contrasting frictional properties within the fault core. Each is thought to affect earthquake nucleation and arrest, yet their effects on preparatory processes before failure and on earthquake recurrence remains insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted direct shear experiments on binary mixtures of soda-lime glass beads and quartz powder, systematically varying the gouge composition from 100 to 0 wt% glass beads at 313 ± 15 kPa normal stress. Frictionally contrasting phases are intermixed at the grain scale, making the mixtures spatially homogeneous but compositionally heterogeneous. Homogeneous glass beads, as one end member of the gouge mixtures, produce quasi-periodic stick-slip with pronounced pre-failure dilation, late-stage rapid slip acceleration, and time and slip predictable recurrence. In contrast, compositionally mixed gouges accelerate more gradually and exhibit shorter dilational phases with small amplitudes. Furthermore, preparatory slip starts earlier in the interseismic period and evolves towards an intermittent critical stress state prior to failure, which is associated with increasing deviation from time-predictable recurrence and a growing fraction of aseismically accommodated slip. The transition from stick-slip to stable sliding occurs within a narrow compositional range (80–85 wt% glass beads), with peak slip velocities differing by approximately 3.8 orders of magnitude between the two regimes. These results demonstrate that gouge composition strongly affects preparatory processes, and predictability of stick-slip recurrence in the laboratory and potentially in nature.
3cb7247b63f68e44: Understanding how small earthquakes rupture in fault systems is central to revealing the physical processes that govern faulting in the Earth’s crust. These events are commonly assumed to be dominated by simple shear slip, producing earthquake sources that can be described by classical double-couple models. This assumption underpins many interpretations of seismicity but has rarely been tested using comprehensive source representations for large numbers of small events. Here we demonstrate that small earthquakes in a well-instrumented fault system systematically depart from double-couple behavior. By applying full earthquake source inversions to thousands of events recorded by a dense seismic network in western Japan, we identify widespread non-double-couple rupture patterns that cluster spatially and exhibit combined shear and opening motions. These observations indicate that non-double-couple processes are a common feature of small-earthquake rupture rather than rare anomalies. Our findings suggest that fluid-related processes, structural complexity and rock damage within fault zones could influence earthquake nucleation and rupture growth. These findings provide further insights into the complexity of small earthquakes in fault systems and their implications for earthquake rupture physics.
e03f61410ab777af: Seismic radiated energy is fundamental to earthquake physics, yet its scaling remains debated. Two conflicting views—magnitude‐invariant apparent stress and systematically increasing apparent stress—have persisted partly because source spectral estimates are poorly constrained. Poorly constrained source spectra also create a long‐standing problem for seismic hazard assessment: many estimates imply ground‐motion variability substantially larger than observed. We show that addressing this inconsistency for peak ground velocity (PGV) yields an independent constraint on radiated‐energy scaling. For crustal earthquakes in Japan ( M w 3.4–7.5), apparent stress increases with magnitude for small‐to‐moderate earthquakes but becomes nearly constant above M w 5–6, reconciling the previously conflicting views. Our source spectral estimates reproduce both the scaling and variability of observed PGV, supporting the inferred apparent‐stress scaling. Regional comparisons further support a similar scaling transition. This transition may reflect enhanced dynamic weakening due to thermal pressurization. PGV consistency provides a stringent quality‐control criterion for radiated‐energy estimates.
420b35e8f7b5def2: This dataset contains relocated hypocenter and centroid locations (Figure 2) and finite-fault slip distributions (Figure 4) associated with the 2021 Mw 7.0 Miyagi-Oki earthquake and surrounding events. The data accompany Yoshida et al. (2026), Geophysical Research Letters, https://doi.org/10.1029/2026GL125835. File descriptions and units are provided in the README.
5b5141b92f8a20f6: The multi‐segment ruptures of the 2023 7.8 and 7.6 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes caused extensive deformation across the entire width of the East Anatolian Fault Zone (Türkiye). To understand how this earthquake doublet could affect such a large region, we model coseismic slip for both earthquakes using surface deformation measurements. We use a Bayesian framework to obtain uncertainties and constrain the significance of our findings. Our model suggests that most of the coseismic slip distributes above 20 km depth with a shallow slip deficit ratio varying along strike from 10% to 80%. Slip is segmented along strike, with higher values on relatively straight segments and decreases at geometric complexities. We also construct postseismic InSAR displacement time series and find that segments with the most afterslip are located at the northeastern end of both ruptures. Aftershocks are usually located along the fault planes, except at the southwestern tip of both ruptures where they spread in wide fan‐shaped zones. These observations can be related to the relative geometric complexity of the southwestern termination of both earthquakes, where extensive crustal damage could have stopped the rupture. Finally, by visualizing the localization of interseismic deformation, we depict the role of strain partitioning between subparallel strike‐slip faults in the unusually large spatial extent of the Kahramanmaraş doublet. These findings highlight the seismic hazard posed by similar tectonic structures in other broad plate boundaries.
527a91af2a87b984: Uplift and widespread Late Miocene‐present magmatism in Anatolia are commonly attributed to lithospheric thinning, possibly facilitated by the arrival of hot mantle plume material. There are various lines of evidence for thin present‐day lithosphere, but the spatial extent and degree of lithospheric thinning and the underlying mantle temperatures remain debated. Here we apply a Bayesian thermo‐compositional approach that jointly inverts surface‐wave dispersion, elevation and surface heat flow for temperatures of the lithosphere and underlying mantle to 360 km depth. Our results reveal that thermal lithospheric thickness across the study region is generally thin, 40–85 km, with thicker lithosphere (>70 km) beneath the Central Pontides and northernmost Arabia and exceptionally thin (40–55 km) lithosphere beneath the Eastern Pontides and the region between the Central and Eastern Anatolian Plateaus. Furthermore, we find a pronounced west‐to‐east increase in mantle potential temperature of ∼140C across 35E. The sharp mantle temperature gradient implies that any inflow of hot plume material is largely confined to the east and therefore is unlikely to be a primary driver of Anatolia's westward motion. The pervasively thin but variable lithospheric thickness indicates widespread, yet heterogeneous lithospheric removal, with the influx of hot mantle material potentially enhancing thinning beneath eastern Anatolia.
d96daa426f07ba89: Accurate retrieval of coseismic deformation fields from Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar is critical for constraining fault slip distributions and assessing seismic hazards. However, extracting pure deformation signals from single‐frame interferograms remains challenging due to the complex coupling of atmospheric turbulence, stratified delays, Digital Elevation Model residuals, orbital errors, and decorrelation noise, particularly in regions lacking external auxiliary data or extensive temporal archives. To address this, we propose Coseis‐Diff, an error‐correction model that requires no external auxiliary data at inference time, built upon a residual denoising diffusion framework. We employ a diffusion transformer backbone, which leverages global self‐attention mechanisms to overcome the limited receptive field of traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This architecture enables the unified correction of multi‐scale errors while preserving the topological continuity of deformation fringes. Evaluation on physics‐based synthetic data sets demonstrates that Coseis‐Diff achieves higher fidelity than CNN baselines. Furthermore, validation on real‐world earthquakes ( M w 5.7–7.05) confirms that the model effectively separates spatially correlated artifacts and reliably recovers deformation signals even in severe low‐coherence zones. Comparisons against an independent Okada dislocation model and GNSS coseismic displacements further show that the recovered phase unwraps more reliably and agrees more closely with these independent observations than the raw interferogram. By replacing the reliance on external corrections or time‐series stacking with physics‐based learned priors, Coseis‐Diff provides a rapid, high‐precision solution for emergency response and source mechanism inversion in data‐scarce environments.
02798eb58c7cc376: We investigate co‐ and post‐seismic P ‐wave velocity ( V p ) changes following the July 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest strike‐slip earthquake using time‐lapse tomography from 50,345 P ‐wave arrivals (2011–2024). Co‐seismically, V p changes correspond to the volumetric strain change lobes of the earthquake, increasing in compressional zones and decreasing in tensional zones. Post‐seismically, V p changes exhibit a reverse pattern, suggesting ongoing subsurface recovery. Notably, the Coso volcanic field, although distal to the rupture, shows significant co‐seismic velocity reduction and rapid post‐seismic recovery, likely indicating fluid migration or poroelastic effects. These results reveal the complex mechanical and hydrological responses to co‐seismic stress changes and provide important insights into post‐seismic healing processes. Our findings offer robust seismic evidence for the response of material properties to crustal deformation, contributing to improved understanding of structure changes in the earthquake process.
e0886c5aaab3d5e8: To understand what governs earthquake size, we investigated the 2021 Mw 7.0 Japan Trench earthquake, which began near a nest of repeating earthquakes. High‐precision hypocenter relocation and P‐waveform correlation show that the mainshock initiated nearly identically to Mw 3.8 repeaters. Waveform deconvolution reveals that, after breaking the Mw 3.8 patch within 0.1 s, the mainshock rupture cascaded through Mw 5–6 patches within 2 s and into the main slip area at 3–6 s. Four preceding Mw 5.1–6.1 events, some with higher initial moment rates, did not rupture this main area, likely because the locked region remained too far from failure. Their repeated occurrence may reflect progressive unlocking of this region. In 2021, a start nearly identical to Mw 3.8 repeaters cascaded hierarchically into an Mw 7.0 rupture, suggesting that earthquake size depends less on how rupture begins than on whether surrounding locked regions are ready to fail.
08418dca0f7abfec: Variations in melt supply can shift slow and ultraslow ridges between magmatic and tectonic accretion modes, but whether this effect persists at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge remains unclear. The eastern Gakkel Ridge provides a critical test because it spreads at only ∼6–10 mm/yr yet shows anomalously strong magmatism. We reconstruct sediment thickness and residual basement across the Eurasian Basin using seismic constraints and time‐dependent sedimentation models for the poorly constrained eastern Nansen Basin. Most of the western Eurasian Basin shows deep residual basement and variable flank asymmetry, consistent with magma‐poor ultraslow accretion. Eastward, residual basement becomes progressively shallower and more symmetric. In the eastern Nansen Basin, shallow residual basement persists even under maximum sedimentation, indicating sustained crustal thickening on both conjugate flanks since ∼45 Ma. These results show that enhanced melt supply can shift oceanic crustal accretion toward a near‐symmetric, magma‐dominated mode even at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge.
a620eadf189832fb: Due to the growth of data volumes in monitoring seismicity, automation is crucial to fully use the information content. Seismic event detection is the first step in processing, aimed at reducing the amount of data by extracting intervals with seismic activity. At the same time, interpretability remains important for justification and quality control of the detected events, especially when multiple candidate events are to be triaged. A novel seismic event detection technique based on cluster analysis of trimmed spectrograms (CATS) was proposed. It used an automatic noise estimator, block-extended d-dimensional amplitude trimmed estimator (B-E-DATE), and cluster filtering in the time-frequency domain. CATS workflow was fully transparent, offering a framework for comprehensive quality control. Evaluated on the benchmark data set TXED, CATS showed competitive performance compared to traditional and deep-learning methods by showing high recall, precision, and F-scores. Furthermore, CATS can be extended to multistation processing and used directly for denoising without requiring any extra parameters, and its outputs can be used for phase picking and event classification.
e9714d6ac64cbe96: Seismic data obtained after stacking or migration typically exhibit low dominant frequency, sparse spatial and temporal sampling, and may retain a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) even after stacking. To enhance the resolution of seismic data, we propose a deep learning-based single-step super-resolution (SR) method that simultaneously performs denoising, interpolation, and frequency extrapolation. We design a seismic data super-resolution Transformer (SDST) to extract and fuse local and global features from low-resolution seismic data, with particular emphasis on the amplitude characteristics and spatial continuity of effective events (e.g., horizons, folds, faults). Edge information from the input data is extracted using the Canny algorithm and used as a mask to generate an edge map, which is then concatenated with the raw data to form a two-channel input, thereby improving amplitude preservation and noise suppression. The SDST backbone comprises residual groups containing Swin Transformer layers which capture features within windows while reducing the computational cost of self-attention by restricting attention to finite-sized windows. Pixel shuffle layers are employed to efficiently upsample the output feature maps from the SDST backbone, thereby enhancing the details of geological structures. In addition, upsampling the input data through a skip connection helps preserve the output amplitudes, particularly for weak events. We prepare 3-dimensional (3D) synthetic seismic volumes with complex geological structures, half of which contain a mixture of strong- and weak-amplitude events. 2-dimensional (2D) slices are then randomly selected from these volumes to construct training datasets that better approximate the characteristics of field data for supervised learning. Numerical tests on both synthetic and field data from different exploration regions demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method.
06fcf1a9b45d152f: Conventional models attribute anomalously high Poisson's ratios in Earth's interior to the presence of fluids or melts. Here, we propose a fundamentally different mechanism, which is rooted in the unique crystal chemistry of lawsonite (CaAl 2 Si 2 O 7 (OH) 2 ·H 2 O). Our high‐pressure and room temperature experiments reveal anomalous changes in the elastic tensor of lawsonite at ∼4.5 and ∼9 GPa, which are linked to phase transitions involving hydrogen‐bond reorganization. Compared to typical mantle minerals, lawsonite exhibits moderately low P‐wave velocity ( V P ) and very low S‐wave velocity ( V S ). More notably, it is characterized by exceptionally high isotropic aggregate Poisson's ratio (0.32–0.38) and V P / V S ratio (1.92–2.27), which serve as diagnostic identifiers in the interpretation of seismic models. In hot subduction zones, such as Cascadia and Southwest Japan, lawsonite provides a key mineralogical mechanism for the high‐Poisson's‐ratio anomalies observed at 20–50 km depth, presenting a viable explanation distinct from conventional models that invoke overpressurized, fluid‐saturated oceanic crust. In colder subduction systems such as NE Japan, the presence of 20–40 vol.% lawsonite can account for the seismic anomalies observed at 50–90 km depth. Furthermore, lawsonite exhibits strong velocity anisotropy, which may help interpret the observed seismic anisotropy. The seismologically unique signature of lawsonite and its compatibility with seismic models underscore how this mineral could have a critical role in facilitating water transport into the deep mantle.
d72f444fc491f38e: Deep-learning denoising is increasingly used for earthquake monitoring, and time–frequency mask-reconstruction models such as DeepDenoiser have shown strong potential for seismic waveform recovery. However, many existing approaches still rely on U-Net-like backbones, leaving the contribution of denoising-specific architectural design insufficiently isolated. Here, we introduce SEQNet, an architecture-focused seismic waveform denoising model that integrates multiscale feature attention (MFA) and global feature aggregation (GFA) into a phase-sensitive time–frequency mask-reconstruction framework. MFA refines encoder features through multiscale context and attention, whereas GFA incorporates bottleneck-level global summaries before decoding. Using paired event–noise waveforms from INSTANCE and STEAD with physical-event-level separation, matched ablation experiments identify MFA as the most strongly supported architectural contribution, while the aggregate effect of GFA is smaller and metric-dependent. Compared with DeepDenoiser and representative conventional methods, SEQNet shows a more favorable reference-based waveform-fidelity profile, whereas DeepDenoiser often produces stronger event-to-pre-event contrast. Trace-level analysis further shows that contrast enhancement and waveform fidelity can disagree on the same records, and a four-day continuous Lushan aftershock test examines downstream phase-picking behavior in continuous data. These results show that targeted architectural modifications can improve waveform-oriented seismic denoising and that module attribution should distinguish waveform fidelity from contrast enhancement.
983475974317af2a: The 2025 M7.8 Mandalay earthquake ruptured ~480 km of the Sagaing Fault, producing one of the longest strike-slip events documented and impacting a vulnerable region. Here we combine remote sensing observations and numerical modeling to show that the subsurface fault geometry and slip distribution could be anticipated from pre-event observations. Along-strike variations in coseismic and interseismic deformation reveal a helix-shaped fault geometry. The average coseismic slip equals or exceeds the interseismic slip deficit, consistent with a minimally slip-predictable model. We generate an ensemble of 3D dynamic rupture models, constrained by the best-fit static slip model, then discriminate among them using independent space-geodetic, seismic, and near-field video observations. The preferred scenario begins bilaterally, then transitions to unilateral southward supershear propagation at depth, while shallow rupture remains subshear. These dynamics are shaped by localized stress heterogeneity and low fracture energy, characteristic of a structurally mature fault zone. Our approach can inform rupture scenarios in understudied regions.
edf1401fddca9a19: Crustal-scale strike-slip zones within transform plate boundaries, as imaged by seismic reflection profiles, commonly appear as low-reflectivity zones in the crust and at the Moho, often overprinted by younger deformation phases. To investigate the geophysical characteristics of fossil strike-slip plate boundaries and assess whether features formed during the initial strike-slip stage are preserved at depth, we study the Gondwana–Laurussia plate boundary zone in Central Europe. We integrate two-dimensional seismic reflection and potential-field data with surface geological information and constraints from basement wells. Based on geophysical characteristics, we subdivide the Saxo-Thuringian Zone, south of the Gondwana–Laurussia boundary zone, into three domains. The northwestern and southeastern domains display high-amplitude, continuous reflections and are interpreted as high-strain domains. The northwestern domain is further interpreted as a strike-slip-dominated region overprinted by late Variscan shortening, analogous to structures exposed in the northwestern Bohemian Massif and the Mid-German Crystalline Zone. In contrast, the Central-domain displays low–amplitude, discontinuous reflections and is interpreted as a low-strain domain bounded by high-strain domains. Although our geophysical observations are dominated by late Variscan compression that overprinted the strike-slip phase, they retain characteristics that allow the identification of a fossil transform plate boundary zone.
e62e2cb7f347338a: Summary Traffic-induced seismic waves provide valuable signals for characterizing the subsurface structures. The operation of metro systems generates powerful, broadband, and repetitive seismic signals that propagate in the urban subsurface. This repeatability mainly arises from scheduled metro operations on fixed tunnel routes with similar metro wagons, speed, and weights. Unlike other traffic signals that are generated by vehicles running on the free surface, the metro operates in subsurface tunnels. The use of metro-induced signals for the estimation of the subsurface model, however, remains unexplored. This paper proposes a metro seismic interferometry workflow for urban subsurface characterization. We analyse the characteristics of metro signals and derive a formula for the stationary-phase zone (SPZ) analysis of metro sources. Empirical Green’s functions (EGFs) are estimated by selecting segments of metro signals when the metro is in the SPZ. We performed a field study in Wuhan, China, by deploying a seismic survey line approximately 70° to a metro line. The EGFs reconstructed from multi-component metro seismic signals show distinct Rayleigh and Love waves. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the EGFs is further improved by stacking multiple metro events. The SNR and the accuracy of the dispersion curves estimated from the EGFs with SPZ analysis are much higher than those obtained without SPZ analysis, demonstrating the validity of our proposed method. The comparison with dispersion curves obtained from road traffic signals shows the reliability of the proposed method. In addition, the EGFs also contain abundant guided P waves with high SNR, enabling the reconstruction of the P-wave velocity model. This work shows that utilizing metro seismic waves provide a powerful, efficient, and cost-effective approach for the estimation and monitoring of urban subsurface models.
16730cf5b060ce9c: The Alpine Fault (AF) is the major plate boundary crustal structure in New Zealand (NZ), producing large-to-great (M7-8+) earthquakes approximately every 300-500 years, and has long been a focal point for earthquake resilience in NZ. This study advances prior AF ground-motion modelling by considering multi-segment ruptures that initiate on the AF and rupture northward onto structures in the Marlborough Fault Zone (MFZ), resulting in ground shaking of consequential amplitudes for the upper South Island and Lower North Island, including Wellington city. From the 2022 NZ National Seismic Hazard Model (NSHM), three multi-segment rupture geometries including the Wairau, Clarence, and Hope fault structures in the MFZ are obtained, together with their scenario rupture rates. Hybrid broadband simulations using a multi-segment kinematic source description and a 3D NZ crustal velocity model are performed. Three rupture realizations per geometry are considered to compare the effects of kinematic rupture randomness with those of the different geometries. To provide comparisons with the prior ground-motion simulations used for public outreach in the AF8 programme, we also simulated the segmented M7.9 Alpine Fiordland-to-Kelly rupture geometry of Bradley et al. (2017a), adopting the same southern hypocentre location in all rupture scenarios, enabling examination of differences due to eight years of advancements in kinematic rupture and crustal velocity modelling. Results illustrate strong northward directivity and basin response, with the largest Wellington amplitudes resulting from the Alpine-Wairau and Alpine-Clarence scenarios -- peak ground accelerations of approximately 0.1 g, comparable to those observed during the 2016 Kaikōura earthquake; in aggregate, these Alpine-MFZ ruptures have a likelihood similar to the conventionally-considered Wellington Fault and Hikurangi subduction sources.
427e5e56199ef7dd: Although substantial gas emissions from postearthquake rupture zones have been documented, their underlying mechanisms, sources, and fault-related migration pathways remain uncertain. Here, we present a systematic tectonogeochemical survey across the surface rupture zone of the 1975 Ms 7.3 Haicheng earthquake, northeast China. A total of 233 sampling sites were established for soil gas concentration measurements, among which nine were further selected for carbon isotope analysis. Synchronous in situ measurements of Rn, CO2, and H2 concentrations were performed at all sites to elucidate the spatial coupling between soil gas concentration anomalies, seismic activity, and fault structures. The results indicate that soil gas concentrations along the rupture zone remain higher than those in background areas 50 yr after the Haicheng earthquake. The peak concentrations of Rn, CO2, and H2 reach 376.60 kBq/m3, 9.98 vol.%, and 1292.00 ppm, respectively, implying distinct geochemical anomalies along the fault zone. The carbon isotope results reveal that the contribution of deep-derived CO2 ranges from approximately 5% to 12%, indicative of the potential upward migration of deep crustal fluids. According to the analysis of gas emission-controlling factors, fault offset, persistent small-to-moderate seismicity, and deep fluid activity are likely the primary controls on these geochemical anomalies. Furthermore, the pronounced H2 anomalies and unique geological conditions of the Haicheng area may be useful for regional geochemical screening of fault-controlled gas migration. In conclusion, this study provides a representative case for understanding decadal-scale postseismic gas migration and its primary controls along the rupture zone of a major continental earthquake.
62a571f8f20ecc69: The Earth’s uppermost inner core (IC) is a critical boundary region where thermal, compositional, and mechanical interactions between the liquid outer-core and solid IC influence solidification processes and the geodynamo. Previous studies relied primarily on PKIKP–PKiKP seismic phases recorded at epicentral distances of 130°–142°. Here, we introduce a complementary approach by analyzing PKIKPPKIKP–PKiKPPKiKP differential times near 90° from deep earthquakes. These rare, multiply reflected phase pairs sample the IC on both descending and ascending paths and share similar trajectories, minimizing the influence of mantle heterogeneity. We measure their differential arrival times via waveform cross correlation in the 0.7–2 Hz frequency band and compute residuals with respect to synthetic seismograms that account for earthquake source mechanisms. These residuals are directly sensitive to P-wave velocity anomalies in the IC. In addition, we identify a new small set of PKIKPPKIKP and PKPbcPKPbc arrivals near 60°, which could support future studies of deeper IC regions. Statistical analysis using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria favors a single-parameter isotropic model, suggesting that the observed residuals can be explained without introducing additional anisotropy. Our results highlight the untapped value of rare, multiply reflected core phase pairs in probing Earth’s deep interior.
7871cf72cf9234f3: The coda moment magnitude (Mwo) has recently been proposed based on the long-period and long-lasting coda energy of large earthquakes. In this study, we perform a systematic evaluation of the Mwo method on its robustness and applicability using a large dataset of 132 large earthquakes from January 2000 to March 2023. The results demonstrate that the Mwo is in general agreement with the moment magnitude (Mw) from the Global Centroid Moment Tensor, with the former being slightly larger. For relatively smaller events (Mw<8.3), the residual between the Mwo and Mw increases with decreasing magnitude. Further synthetic tests indicate that the background noise (or the signal-to-noise-ratio) is the primary factor for the deviation of Mwo for smaller events. After comparing different approaches, we propose an empirical relationship to correct the Mwo for events with Mw<8.3. Examination of other potential influences reveals a minimal impact, showing the robustness of the corrected Mwo and the enhanced Mwo method retains the advantages of potentially capturing a broader portion of the seismic energy release. Its stability has been shown to be largely insensitive to variations in epicenter location and the number of stations and to be only mildly sensitive to changes in source focal mechanisms and depth of hypocenter. Furthermore, the improved method is applicable to earthquakes with Mw≥7.3 when a sufficient number of high-quality coda measurements is available, with the recommended and more robust operational range being Mw≥7.5, thereby extending its capability for accurate magnitude determination of large earthquakes.
4cc41614cde9b40d: Distinguishing small earthquakes from anthropogenic seismic sources is important for accurate fault characterization and seismic hazard assessment, yet remains challenging in regions with sparse seismic networks and frequent quarry activities. Around Atlanta, Georgia, only a small number of local natural earthquakes and one operator-confirmed quarry blast in July 2026 are reported in regional USGS catalogs in recent years. Here we use three cataloged earthquakes and the 2026 quarry blast as references to search 14 years of continuous seismic and pressure records at a nearby permanent station N4.Y52A. Based on a machine-learning-assisted workflow, we identify 2,181 impulsive events with clear seismic arrivals, associated pressure disturbances, and reliable particle-motion measurements. Most of them occur during weekday working hours and exhibit repeated source-distance and directional patterns that correspond to known quarry areas, indicating that the detected population is dominated by quarry-blast activity. The search also recovers smaller earthquake candidates and short event sequences with more ambiguous origins, demonstrating that waveform similarity or occurrence time alone cannot determine source type. As an independent case study, we reassess signals previously associated with a 17 July 2023 spontaneous rock exfoliation event at Arabia Mountain. The previously associated regional signal is more consistent with quarry activity, whereas subsequent exfoliation events in 2024 produced highly localized signals recorded only by a near-source dense array but not clearly at N4.Y52A. These results demonstrate that improved seismic detection must be accompanied by independent seismic, acoustic, spatial, and direct observational constraints for reliable source identification.
