Neural reparametrization offers an alternative means of improving inversion robustness without switching objective functions, but existing methods often converge slowly and struggle to recover fine-scale details. In addition, static positional encoding (SPE) may introduce high-frequency instability if improperly configured. To address this limitation, we propose an Adaptive Neural Reparametrization Dispersion Spectrum Inversion (ANR-DSI) method. The subsurface velocity model is reparametrized by a coordinate-based multilayer perceptron (MLP), and an adaptive positional encoding (APE) mechanism is incorporated whose frequency weights are updated through gradients propagated from the physical forward operator. By promoting a coarse-to-fine optimization trajectory, this dynamic mechanism enhances inversion robustness by stabilizing large-scale structures first, while simultaneously accelerating the learning of fine-scale features. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively mitigates the inversion’s dependence on the initial model, accelerates convergence relative to standard neural reparametrization, and maintains stable performance under noisy conditions. Furthermore, application to a real-world urban distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) dataset confirms its immense potential for near-surface imaging in practical scenarios.
c1744db19c81ef4f: Key questions remain on how strain localization and weakening occur along shear zones. The Hulw Shear Zone (Saih Hatat, Oman Mountains) allows the exhumation of blueschist facies continental units. This shear zone displays mode I and hybrid veins coeval to a mylonitic foliation, developed from epidote‐blueschist to low‐greenschist facies conditions. A strain gradient corresponds to the development of a S‐C‐C′ fabric and a modal enrichment in muscovite and pyrophyllite, matched by a progressive increase in their physical interconnectivity. Microstructural analysis suggests that interconnected shear planes formed due to the interplay between fracturing and ductile deformation. These planes allowed fluid to flow preferentially along the newly formed fractures and precipitate phyllosilicates. Interconnected bands of small quartz grains are in contact with phyllosilicates, suggesting preferential recrystallization. Preferential grain boundary sliding occurred at the quartz‐phyllosilicate interfaces, with precipitation of new phyllosilicates in dilatant sites. Diffuse microfracturing also occurred at high‐angle to the shear planes, evidenced in quartz grains by fluid inclusion bands. Pyrophyllite and muscovite display kinking and fracturing, are intergrown down to the submicron scale and display truncated boundaries, reflecting dissolution and precipitation mechanisms. We propose that diffuse microfracturing can cyclically enhance the permeability of shear zones, promoting the nucleation of weak mineral phases. These mechanisms weaken the rock volume, localize strain and facilitate exhumation. Diffuse microfracturing allows fluids to transiently migrate perpendicularly to main anisotropies and fluid barriers, such as phyllosilicate‐rich rocks. These microstructures might represent a geological record of slow earthquakes forming during the exhumation of the subducted continental crust.
516edc21cf2d13b3: Understanding volcanic unrest episodes and determining whether they will escalate to hazardous eruptions is a key research goal for improving volcano monitoring procedures. Ruapehu volcano, one of the most active in Aotearoa New Zealand, underwent a significant period of unrest in 2022 that was characterized by high levels of seismic tremor and a heating cycle in the summit crater lake. The tremor was notable for featuring prolonged periods of “drumbeats” as well as harmonic tremor. Conventional methods of earthquake location estimations struggle to locate the source due to the emergent nature of the tremor as well as the relatively sparse seismic network around the volcano. Here we use the network covariance matrix method to isolate and locate the tremor source within the volcano. Our results suggest low‐level tremor commenced 3 months prior to the unrest episode, coinciding with a brief earthquake swarm at similar depths. Tremor and drumbeats during the unrest episode were continuously located at shallow (
61e94c0d443e5eba: Volcanic surface deformation is a primary indicator of subsurface magmatic processes, yet the mechanisms driving subsidence following periods of unrest in the absence of eruption remain debated. Changbaishan volcano, which has exhibited decadal subsidence since its 2002–2005 unrest episode, exemplifies this problem. Here, we integrate Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar observations with three‐dimensional thermo‐mechanical modeling constrained by gravity, seismic, and magnetotelluric data to examine a possible gravity‐driven mechanism. Our results indicate that the observed subsidence is best reproduced by the gravitational settling of a dense, mafic melt core embedded within a shallow, lower‐density felsic mush reservoir within the tested model framework. The preferred model reproduces the observed deformation magnitude and is consistent with the spatial association among subsidence, relatively high gravity anomalies, and high‐conductivity anomalies. These results suggest that post‐unrest subsidence at Changbaishan can be attributed to negative buoyancy resulting from internal density heterogeneity, while alternative or mixed mechanisms cannot be fully excluded. Similar associations among subsidence, gravity anomalies and conductive or low‐velocity structures at volcanoes such as Askja and Aluto provide potential analogs for future testing of this mechanism.
fd5e810f73c18d13: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.
63143b90826be318: Basal channels, troughs carved into ice shelf bases by buoyant plumes, modulate basal melt and can weaken ice shelves. Through hydrostatic adjustment they have a surface expression, yet their geometry is largely mapped manually, limiting the number of channels studied and the consistency between mappings. We present Sub-Ice, a semi-automated tool that maps basal channels from surface digital elevation models. From user-defined start and end points, Sub-Ice traces the channel centerline by iteratively locating elevation minima, extracts cross-sectional profiles and delineates channel edges using one of three methods (slope threshold, profile knee point or peak prominence), producing georeferenced centerlines and edges and along-channel width and depth. Applied to 34 channels on Roi Baudouin Ice Shelf, East Antarctica, Sub-Ice centerlines differ from manually digitized ones by a median of 132 m, at the upper end of the differences between manual records from different years (74-132 m), while following the channel trough more closely. Absolute channel widths depend on the edge method and the width of the edge search window, which we calibrate against a slope-based criterion. Rather than seeking a single "true" edge, Sub-Ice applies explicit, reproducible criteria, enabling consistent comparison of channel geometry across channels, ice shelves and time.
1aa0b4b583fa08c0: Rock permeability changes dramatically during brittle deformation, affecting faulting dynamics and crustal fluid flow. Here, we combine fluid-flow and local pore-pressure measurements acquired during a quasi-static shear-failure test in Westerly granite with a three-dimensional finite-element inverse method. The measured flow rate and six internal pore pressures constrain the local hydraulic transmissivities (permeability-thickness products) of ten cells along the growing fault. Synthetic ensembles anchored to the pressure-sensor accuracy recover these transmissivities with median mean errors of 7-9%, with the fault ends generally better resolved than the interior. Applied to the experiment, the method resolves episodic transmissivity increases, interspersed with decreases, through fault growth and slip. Local values reach approximately $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ m$^3$ (16 times the bulk contribution), and the final-stage values vary by a factor of 2.3 along the fault. Across cells, the median absolute change in recovered transmissivity is at most about 16% for $\pm50\%$ changes in assumed fault-zone thickness. The local one-dimensional estimates of Aben et al. (2024) agree in scale with the three-dimensional results, with a median 3-D/apparent ratio of 0.81. Cumulative acoustic-emission counts track the overall hydraulic evolution, but the relations of local event density, its stagewise increments and amplitude-weighted activity to transmissivity vary between cells. The comparison distinguishes the value of AE for mapping damage growth from quantitative hydraulic prediction using event-count and relative-amplitude metrics.
4a4ce2d291d73113: Distributed volcanic fields are hazardous and poorly understood. They display enigmatic spatio-temporal patterns, with varying degrees of alignment and clustering that lack a clear explanation; the locations of their magma sources and underlying geodynamic processes also often remain uncertain. We propose a method to constrain the magma source feeding eruptive vents by tracing magma pathways in reverse, from the vents through the crust to the depth of magma generation inferred geochemically. The approach involves first constraining the stress field by numerically modelling the primary stress mechanisms; then, a trajectory model backtracks magma pathways, aligning them perpendicular to the local axis of least compression, also accounting for magma buoyancy. We show the potential of this method at the Auckland Volcanic Field, New Zealand, which comprises at least 53 vents and an undefined source location. We identify (weak) regional extension and unloading of the adjacent Hauraki Rift as the dominant stress factors. The computed reversed magma pathways initially descend subvertically beneath the AVF, then tilt and become subhorizontal, ultimately converging at ~30-70 km depth beneath the offshore Hauraki Rift. Simulations suggest that the variability in vent distribution within the AVF may stem from perturbations in the relative contributions of different stress sources and that magma ascent may be slow at depth, where trajectories are subhorizontal, and relatively fast during the late-stage, near-vertical ascent period, consistent with previous geochemical analyses of erupted scoria. Magma pathway retrogression offers a new approach to illuminate the deep origins of volcanic fields.
f7d3eff2baac3903: Understanding Earth's core requires accurate descriptions of multicomponent iron alloys under extreme conditions. Here, we develop the Earth's Core Atomistic Model (ECAM) for Fe-Ni-S-Si-O-C-H alloys through sampling with a foundational atomistic model, targeted ab initio simulations, and iterative exploration. A compact dataset selected from nearly half a million configurations is consistently labeled using high-accuracy first-principles calculations and used to train a lightweight model. The model explicitly includes thermal electronic contributions and runs nearly two orders of magnitude faster than the original foundational model. ECAM corrects artifacts in the foundational model's description of core materials and reproduces the density, seismic velocity, Gibbs free energy, and phase diagrams of Fe and binary alloys in agreement with previous ab initio calculations. ECAM is expected to enable more realistic modeling of chemical partitioning and crystallization in Earth's core. Our workflow also provides a practical route from foundational-model sampling to efficient domain-specific simulation.
36e4201b13b02d2c: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.
826527551ae92eb5: Natural disasters that devastate human societies can also alter Earth's rotation. The 2011 $M_w$ 9.1 Tōhoku earthquake, one of the most powerful earthquakes ever recorded, shortened the day by 1.80 microseconds. Tropical cyclones are the costliest weather disasters, yet whether they can alter Earth's rotation remains unknown. Here we use atmospheric reanalysis to estimate, and numerical simulations to confirm, that a landfalling tropical cyclone can transiently alter the length of day by amounts rivalling those by great earthquakes. For example, Hurricanes Harvey (2017) and Katrina (2005) lengthened the day by 1.87 microseconds and 2.29 microseconds, respectively. As the climate warms, tropical cyclones may become an increasingly important source of variability in Earth's rotation.
e87c788f2293d018: Seismic performance assessment relies on computationally expensive nonlinear simulations, limiting uncertainty quantification and inference of structural properties from observed responses. We develop a manifold-based generative framework that learns the joint distribution of uncertain structural parameters and seismic-response trajectories from limited high-fidelity simulations. Combining Diffusion Maps, score-based Diffusion Modeling, and Geometric Harmonics, the framework enables both forward probabilistic prediction and inverse inference. Applied to a nine-story steel moment-resisting frame, the results reveal which structural properties are identifiable from seismic performance and how uncertainty in these properties influences response. In particular, the learned representation captures post-capping degradation characteristics more effectively than individual strength parameters. Inverse inference identifies distinct structural configurations that produce similar seismic performance, with representative solutions independently validated using nonlinear simulations. These findings demonstrate how generative learning can support uncertainty-aware seismic assessment while revealing structural non-identifiability and alternative mechanisms underlying observed performance
dfe0e728d01be488: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.
f56d0c06b28df1e1: The low absorption of microwaves at L-band in ice enables the retrieval of internal ice sheet parameters from satellite observations. However, knowing the precise value of the ice absorption $κ$a(T ) as a function of temperature is a strict prerequisite. The existing knowledge is well constrained above 2 GHz and under 200 MHz, lacking constraints in the P-and L-bands. In this study, we infer ice absorption values using the spatial variations of L-band radiometric observations across Antarctica and comparing them with internal ice temperature variations through a simple emission model. More importantly, we adopt a probabilistic approach to determine a credible interval for absorption, using a Bayesian retrieval method. Our algorithm seeks the optimal multiplier factor $α$ to apply to the current lowest estimate ice absorption formulation $κ$a(T ) proposed by M{ä}tzler 2006, and computes the probability distribution of $α$. The results show the absorption is most likely 1.5 to 1.7 times higher than this lowest formulation, which reduces the actual sensing depth at L-band.
093ab1f5fd81a7ca: Accurate pressure determination is essential in high pressure experiments. Inconsistencies among pressure scales limit direct comparisons and contribute to uncertainty in measured properties, such as, phase boundaries, melting conditions, and thermodynamic models, especially above 100 GPa where existing scales diverge by >10 GPa. EoSAlign, an open-source software, can calculate, compare, and align pressures using a range of published calibrations. EoSAlign calculates pressure from experimental measurements (such as volume (A^3), Raman shift (cm^-1), or luminescence peak position (nm)) and it can be used to compare pressure values from different pressure standards. Using EoSAlign, we fit and align the bridgmanite and post-perovskite equations of state to a common scale, enabling us to reduce pressure scale related differences. EoSAlign can be applied to any high pressure data analysis to compare experimental results, improve consistency between studies, and advance our understanding of planetary interiors and high pressure physics.
